Area is about 50% improved but improvements on the whole are cheap and not well maintained. City dump is located just off Baxter at corner of McSpadden. Southern Railway Company has large shops at northeast corner of area and formerly employed hundreds of men many of whom lived in the area near the shops, but about 12 years ago the main shops were moved to John Sevier, about 15 miles distant, which took the greater number of these employees away and has resulted in a great decline in this part of area. Several smaller industrial plants in the area have also been abandoned. A low-cost housing project for white people "Western Heights" is now being built in the area at the junction of Jourolman and Virginia. It will provide 244 new units, will cost about $1,256,575 and will rent for approximately $3.00 per room per month. It will be ready for occupancy about May 1940. Area is well served by schools and stores. Transportation is by gasoline bus and is adequate.
Negro school teachers - Mechanics - Common laborers - Domestics - All types of Negro workers

This area is almost entirely occupied by Negroes. It is rolling and about 90% improved. Is within walking distance of principal business center and has all utilities. It contains a conglomeration of small shacks and cottages of varying degrees of repair. In the northern part is located Knoxville College, a Negro college, and some very fair properties are located around it occupied by some of the faculty members of the college. A low-cost housing project for Negroes "College Homes" is now being built just south of the college. It will be completed about June 1940 and will provide about 320 units. Rental will be about $3.00 per room per month. At the south end of the area several industrial plants are located. Some white people live in the southeast corner of the area along Deaderick Street and others but Negroes are gradually getting into this section. In the extreme southeast tip of the area along Main Street and south of it are some large older properties occupied by white people ranging in value from $2500 to $4000, quite a bit in excess of the average of the remainder of the area, but these properties are old and largely used for rooming and boarding houses.
Some infiltration of lower-income group in northern part of area

This is a rolling area, almost 100% improved, within walking distance of principal business center of city, schools, churches and community stores are convenient. The Eastern part of area is very close to main campus of University of Tennessee, it contains many large old homes formerly occupied by wealthy citizens but in recent years have been turned into rooming houses for university students and fraternity houses. The Northern part of the area is near industrial plants located along the railroad tracks just North of the area and some residents in this section work in these plants. The Western part of the area is the more recently improved but construction is somewhat cheap.     Part of area along Cumberland is interspersed with stores, filling stations and other small business establishments.     Age of properties, surrounding influences on north, west and east make this definitely a third grade area.
Business & professional men - executives - white collar workers

This is a small area, rolling to hilly, and about 98% improved. The best part is located on Clinch and White West of 19th Street. The eastern part is the older and is subject to encroachment of rooming and boarding houses for students of the University of Tennessee and Fraternity Houses.     There are a great many four family brick apartments on Laurel Avenue and several larger apartments scattered throughout the area of the better type.     Western part of area contains most of the single-family homes which are generally well constructed of uniform style and architecture. Grade school in area C-4 to the east. Area is within walking distance of principal business center, had adequate transportation by gasoline bus and street car, and is convenient to stores located on Cumberland Avenue. Has all utilities.     Fort Sanders Hospital, a private institution, is located at corner of Clinch and 17th Streets.

This is a rolling area about 80% improved. It is within walking distance of principal business center and also well served by street car and bus transportation. School is located in area, churches and stores very convenient. The Eastern side of the area adjoins the main campus of University of Tennessee, consists mostly of large old homes some of which are fraternity houses and some are used as boarding and rooming houses for university students.     Circle Park, in southeastern corner, is best section of area and contains large, old homes occupied by wealthy citizens, but there are only about a dozen houses in this section and surrounding influences are against it. Western side of area is the more recently improved but construction is somewhat cheap. Railroad track is western boundary and plant of Fulton Sylphon Manufacturing Company is located just across the track from this area. Some residents of the area work in this plant.     Age of properties, surroundings, type of construction make this a third grade area.

This is a rolling area about 98% improved. It has all utilities, is within walking distance of principal business center and well served by street car. Along 17th Street, between Yale and Rose are located several large, expensive homes occupied by some wealthy citizens. The other higher priced properties are located on Lake Avenue, Terrace Avenue, Caledonia and Melrose. Cheaper properties are located on Yale, Lilly and Rose.     Eastern part of area is subject to encroachment of rooming and boarding houses for students of the University of Tennessee, and Fraternity Houses. Schools, stores and churches are convenient and area is a very popular residential section.     Type of improvements, type of population and easy accessibility of center of city will keep this section desirable for many years.

Just a small area of cheap properties occupied by Negroes in a section lying along the river and railroad tracks and back of the University of Tennessee. It is very hilly, about 80% improved with cheap properties. It is occupied largely by Negro laborers and domestics. White people live in the western end of the area. Type of property, population, lack of maintenance and location make it a fourth grade area.
Factory workers in woolen mills - Foundry - Sangravel Material Company

This is a rolling area along the banks of the Tennessee River, only about 40% improved. A textile plant, sangravel plant and a marble plant are located in the area and some residents in the area are employed in these plants. There are some better type of houses located at Blount and Hawthorne. Some small stores located in the area but some distance to schools and churches. Only transportation is by gasoline bus along the highway which is the eastern boundary, but it is only a short distance from the area to the principal business center which lies just across the river.     Poor maintenance of improvements, cheap construction, unstable type of predominating population make this a fourth grade area.

This is the oldest section in South Knoxville - a rolling to hilly area about 80% improved. Sevier Avenue is almost entirely business out to Claude Street and several industrial plants are located north of Sevier, between it and the river - a large lumber and millwork plant, packing plant, laundry and others. Some nice homes of a much better type than the average for the community are located on Phillips between Agee and Daisy. School is located in area, also stores and churches. Not far distant to principal business center. Gasoline bus transportation along Sevier Avenue.     It is a fairly good area, but age of properties, antiquity of architecture, lack of uniform type of improvements make it a fourth grade area.
Marble plants - Bakery - Other industrial workers

This is a rolling to hilly area containing many different types of houses in a section known as "Vestal". It is about 50% improved but predominantly of cheaper type of construction. The southwestern part of the area along Avenue A, B, C and D contains small cheaply constructed houses, 3 and 4 rooms, ranging about $800 to $1200. A small area around Immanuel and Petway is much better, and the same is true of a small area on Goode just off Blount. School and stores located in area, and Young High School, a county school, is not far distant.     Some sections of the area have some very nice homes in it, but the predominating type is of cheap construction, not well maintained and the general characteristics of the community make it a fourth grade area.
Marble workers - Factory workers - Clerical - Wage earners

This is a rolling area located in South Knoxville. Better properties are located on Young Avenue and several homes on this street about 30% higher in value than average for the area. City limits line runs along Young Avenue for a short distance and Young High School (a county high school) is located just outside city limits. Grade school located in area. Children of city residents can attend county high school without paying tuition.     Part of area along state highway is almost entirely vacant - a few scattered rather nice homes and several filling stations being located on it. It is a main traffic artery out of the city to the south and carries a heavy traffic load. There has been some activity in new construction in this area but in the cheaper bracket. Area to the west, cheap construction and location south of the river makes this a third grade area.

This area known as "Lindbergh Forrest" and the subdivision was started about 10 years ago by a speculative builder. It is only about 25% improved, is well laid out in a wooded section, with rolling terrain. Construction is generally good and of uniform style and architecture. Has all utilities but public sewerage. Area has no public transportation and this has some adverse effect. It is only a short distance from the principal business center but is across the Tennessee River. Schools are fairly convenient and community stores are located only a short distance away.     The area is not developed for about 1 block from the Highway although the subdivision extends up to the Highway. On the western side of the highway is shown a red area but the two areas are divided by the four lane highway and land on either side of the highway is only sparsely improved with a few good homes and several filling stations.
Small salaried clerical workers - Mechanics - Wage earners

This area located in South Knoxville, is rolling to hilly and only about 40% improved. Some very nice large homes on Highland Avenue (northern part) - remainder of area consists of small 5-6 room cottage and bungalow type in the cheaper bracket. New school located in area and some small stores also, but some distance to churches and community business center. The part of the area outside city limits has been developed within past 5 years, consists of about 100 houses of fairly uniform construction and well maintained - about 20 new houses built in this section in past year.     Distance to center of city, location on south side of river, and majority of improvements being in cheaper bracket make this a third grade area.
Business men - Jr. executives, white collar workers

This area is known as "Island Home" and is level, about 80% improved. It is a well laid out subdivision, of generally well constructed homes of uniform style and architecture. The area suffers from proximity to Tennessee River, also bad approach through area D-10.     Nearest grade school is located is area D-10 and this is also an objectionable feature - distance to high school is another objection. Area has all utilities and adequate transportation. State School for Deaf adjoins area on southeast. Objectionable features cited and the fact that it is located south of the River make the area a "light blue" area.

A small rolling to hilly area, about 30% developed, located at the edge of the city limits. No sidewalks. School, church and store convenient.     Gilbert Lane is the best street - others contain cheaper properties fairly well maintained. Transportation by gasoline bus at about 3 blocks from northwest corner.     Distance to center of city, lack of restrictions and uniformity, and predominating cheaper construction make this a third grade area.
Industrial workers in furniture factories and Southern Railway Shops.
Built by lot owners for homes

This is an area of fairly uniform constructed cheaper homes, many occupied by industrial workers employed in C.B. Atkin Company furniture manufacturers, located at north end of area, and in Southern Railway Shops, located just a short distance west of the area. It is fairly level and about 85% improved. School is located in area and churches and stores are convenient. Transportation is by gasoline bus along Central Avenue.     In southern part of area along Harvey Street are some very cheap shotgun type of houses. Age of properties, lack of proper maintenance, mixed type of style and construction make this a third grade area.
Factory workers - clerical workers - Wage earners

A level to rolling area about 98% improved - greater portion consisting of small 5-6 room cottage and bungalow type houses averaging about 30 years of age. Grade and high school located in area - it is within walking distance of principal business center. On Glenwood between Luttrell and Scott there are some large old expensive homes formerly occupied by wealthy families but now being turned into small apartments.     Age of properties, antiquity of architecture, completeness of development and infiltration of lower income group make this a third grade area.
Negro laborers - Low-wage earners - Some Negro professional men - Some white mechanics and clerical workers.

This is one of the oldest sections of the city - a rolling to hilly area the western side of which is occupied almost exclusively by Negroes. There is almost every type of house, shacks, cottages and large old 2-story houses, all poorly maintained. It adjoins the principal business center of the city on the west which makes it a popular living place for the poor type of population.     Along Hill and Rouser streets there are white people living and homes are well maintained, of much better type of construction than remainder of area, with values ranging from $2000 to $3500 and renting from $20 to $35 per month. The same condition exists along Main Street to Swan Street except properties are not as well maintained and values not as high.     Better type of Negro population lives on Dandridge, Vine and Bethel. A large Negro high school is located in the area. A low-cost housing project "Austin Homes" for Negroes is to be built on Preston at Vine Street. It will contain 200 units when completed and will cost $839,000. Property has been bought and contract is to be let about middle of December. Construction will take about 12 months from time it is started. 57 units are to be demolished on the site. At Preston and McCallie there are located several large tobacco warehouses which extend south on Preston Street for about two blocks.
Infiltration of Negroes and lower-income group

This area located on a high hill overlooking the Tennessee River and has some very nice homes in it. However, the approach to the area is through a Negro section of very old, dilapidated properties and Negroes and lower income group are gradually getting into this area.     Eastern side contains the cheaper properties and is sparsely improved - as a whole area about 40% improved. Western part contains better properties but surroundings make this a third grade area.     Some distance to white schools and churches.
White-collar workers - some factory workers of Standard Knitting Mills

A level to rolling area about 85% improved. One of the largest textile plants in city from standpoint of number of employees is located in area just north and many of these employees reside in this area.     Better part of area is Fifth, Magnolia and Linden. Cheaper properties in northern stores located in area. Transportation by electric street car and is adequate. Grade school and Junior High School located in area.     Age and type of properties, completeness of development and obsolete type of construction make this a third grade area.
Business & professional men - white collar workers
Gradual infiltration of slightly lower income population
Mostly built by owners of lots for homes

Remaining 5% consists of apartments, 4 to 32 units, 3/5 rooms, brick, average age about 12 years, renting from $35 to $60 per month and valued at about $7500 to $40,000. No sale demand for them but rental demand is good.     This is a rolling area about 80% improved, the vacant part being at the northeast corner, remainder about 100% improved. Magnolia Avenue has many large homes that were very expensive when built, it is a wide street and one of the principal arteries leading from the city to the east and carries a heavy traffic. Most all new construction has been on Woodbine and has been by a speculative builder. Transportation facilities are excellent, churches, schools and community stores convenient. Land values were originally very high in this area, $35 to $70 per front foot, and the section is now competing with comparable section having lot values from $10 to $25 per front foot. It will remain a popular rental area for many years because of its accessibility to principal business center, but because of fading home ownership it can hardly be classed above a "light blue" area.

A level to rolling area consisting largely of small 5-6 room cottage and bungalow type houses, fairly well maintained but of cheaper construction. Amusement Park located on north side of area.     Eastern part is known as "Burlington" and a community business center of some size of area along Abner Street is a small section of very cheap 3-4 room houses that should be classed fourth grade but it is only a very small section. Southern part of area is sparsely developed.     Lack of uniformity of construction, age of properties and cheaper improvements make this a third grade area.     Grade school in area, churches convenient, transportation by electric street car along Magnolia.

The part of this area north of Holston Drive is known as Chilhowee Hills and the part south of Holston Drive is known as Holston Hills. The Chilhowee Hills part is more thickly improved with homes ranging from about $5000 to $7500, well constructed of uniform style and architecture, well maintained - and the Holston Hills part contains the larger, more expensive homes with the larger lots, but is more sparsely improved. The Holston Hills part adjoins the Holston Hills Country Club and Golf Course, the terrain is rolling and well wooded, and has many beautiful building sites. The entire area is about 25% improved.     Area is outside city limits - has all utilities except public sewerage. County grade school is located just across the highway north of the area. Nearest transportation is gasoline bus which stops at city limits and does not reach this area.     Largest volume of new construction within past two years has been in the range from $6000 to $8000. Type of improvements, type of population and popularity of the section as indicated by volume of new construction, makes this a first grade area.

This is just a small area of shacks occupied by Negroes. It is rolling to hilly, about 40% improved. Has all utilities and transportation is by gasoline bus along Broadway. Houses are cheaply built and poorly maintained and there is nothing in the area to recommend it. Because of cheap rent and easy access to transportation no difficulty is experienced in keeping the habitable houses occupied.

This is a rather large area but properties are fairly uniform in style throughout the area. It is rolling to hilly, about 60% improved. Schools are located on both east and west side of area and are convenient to entire area. Transportation is by gasoline bus along Broadway with shuttle bus along Washington Avenue through southeastern part. Broadway is a wide thoroughfare, the main artery to Fountain City and carries a heavy load of traffic. It is dotted with stores, filling stations, sandwich shops, tourist homes, some nice private homes and two nice large apartment houses.     The northeast corner, the eastern side between areas B-7 and B-9, and the western side beyond area B-8 are sparsely developed. It is an area of spotted improvements, some good, some bad and some indifferent. As a whole properties are fairly well maintained. Distance to principal business center is one adverse factor especially to the eastern and northeastern parts of the area.     Most new construction is in eastern and southeastern parts and it is likewise spotted.

This is a small rolling area, about 70% improved, and developed within the past few years of generally well constructed homes of uniform style and architecture. It has all utilities, is adequately served by gasoline bus transportation along Broadway with adequate schedule.     A good grade and junior high school is located just adjoining the northwest corner of the area. Community stores located along Broadway and are convenient. Properties surrounding the area, especially on the north, are much older and cheaper. Uniformity of style and construction, general appearance and maintenance of homes, type of population, and popularity of area as indicated by recent volume of new construction make this particular part a second grade area.
White-collar workers - Wage earners - Truck drivers

A level area of fairly uniformly constructed small cottage and bungalow type homes well maintained, just slightly less desirable than the better area adjoining on the north. It is only about 50% improved. Grade school located in area B-7 adjoining on north - stores located on Broadway - churches some distance away.     Nearest transportation is along Broadway to west and about 4 blocks north of the area and this is one adverse factor. Distance to center of city, lack of adequate transportation and lack of building restrictions make this a third grade area.
Jr. Executives - business & professional men - white collar workers

This is a small area along Fairmont Boulevard and Emoriland Boulevard, consisting of small single-family homes, generally well constructed of uniform style and architecture. The name of Aviation Avenue (extension of Fairmont) has been changed to Fairmont Boulevard and has been continued eastward for about three blocks beyond the city limits and the major portion of new building in the area within past year has been done on Fairmont outside city limits.     Portion inside city has all utilities and outside has all but public sewerage. School is located on Emoriland Boulevard, transportation is by gasoline bus along Broadway with adequate schedules, but eastern part of area is some distance from transportation.     Stores along Broadway and convenient.     It is a good second class area of medium priced homes, well maintained and occupied by a substantial type of people.

This is a rolling area located at the edge of city development. Population in northeast corner is almost entirely Negro. Several lumber mills and a textile mill are located on the railroad tracks running through the center of the area and provide employment for many residents in the area.     Best part of the area is 4 blocks on the west end of Cecil Avenue, the northern boundary of the area. Houses in these 4 blocks are 5-6 room bungalow type valued at about $2000 to $3000 and renting at from $18 to $25 per month. The remainder of the area consists of small shacks and cottages, poorly maintained and cheaply constructed. Small stores in community but some distance to schools. Western end is served by gasoline bus on Broadway but eastern end lacks adequate transportation facilities. Poor maintenance of improvements, cheap construction, isolated location and unstable type of predominant population makes this a fourth grade area.

This area is known as "Indian Hills". It is a beautifully wooded section with rolling terrain and is about 50% improved. Homes are of uniform style and architecture but the subdivision was developed by a speculative builder with a reputation for rather cheap construction, and for this reason there is some sales resistance. Lot values have also suffered a severe decline during recent years.     Grade school is within walking distance and community stores are not far distant. Transportation is by gasoline bus along Washington Pike (North boundary) which connects with bus along Broadway. Distance from center of city adversely affects. Part of area inside city limits has all utilities and part outside has all but public sewerage.     Most new construction has been at northwest corner and on the eastern side of area. It is what might be termed a low second grade area.
White collar workers - some junior executives
Readily - largely built for lot owners

Located in Fountain City, an unincorporated village, and free from Knoxville City taxes. Terrain is rolling, area about 40% improved with medium priced bungalow type homes, well maintained and fairly uniform as to style and architecture. Transportation is by gasoline bus along Broadway with adequate schedule - with western part of area somewhat distant from transportation. Grade school and large county high school located in Area C-3 adjoining, and are within walking distance. Business center of Fountain City is also convenient.     It is an area of good, medium priced homes occupied by a substantial type of people with moderate incomes. It is far enough away from Knoxville to be free from the smoke of the city and yet only 20 minutes automobile time from the main business center of Knoxville and about thirty minutes by bus transportation. Area has all utilities except public sewerage.
Built for lot owners for homes

This area contains the older part of Fountain City, is rolling to hilly and about 75% improved. The business part of Fountain City is located about in the center of the area. Improvements vary from small cottages to large two-story house of frame construction, old but fairly well-maintained. The population is of substantial type.     Grade and county high school are located in area. Transportation to Knoxville is by gasoline bus along Broadway with adequate schedule. Area has all utilities excepting public sewerage, homes having septic tanks.     Southern strip of area along Broadway is dotted with filling stations, beer taverns, soft drink stands and sandwich shops, with some fairly substantial homes. Properties are fairly well constructed on the average but are old and lack uniformity of type and architecture.

This area located in Fountain City, an unincorporated village, and free from Knoxville city taxes. Terrain is rolling, area about 65% improved. Grade school just across Jacksboro Pike in adjoining area and large county high school is located in area C-8, within walking distance. Fountain City business center not far distant.     Transportation is by gasoline bus along Jacksboro Pike with adequate schedule. Has all utilities except public sewerage.     Better part of the area (the 40% part) is located south of Sanders Lane, and the lower priced part (the 60% part) is located in the northern part. Properties along Gibbs and Hillcrest are the older ones (about 15-20 years) and the major portion of the part south of Hillcrest has been built up within past 5 years.     It is a good area of moderate priced bungalow type homes, fairly well constructed of uniform style and architecture and occupied by a substantial type of people of moderate incomes. Volume of new construction during past two years is indicative of popularity of area.
White collar workers - professional men - executives
Practically all built by lot owners for homes

A gently rolling, well wooded area about 30% improved with homes of uniform style and architecture and well constructed. Has all utilities but public sewerage, each house having septic tank. Bus transportation along Tazewell Road and Jacksboro Pike with adequate schedule. Grade school in area and county high school not far distant. Community business center located at junction of Tazewell Road and Jacksboro Pike.     It is located outside city limits, in Fountain City, an unincorporated village, and is free from Knoxville city taxes. Cemetery is located just across Tazewell Road at southeast corner of area.     Lots are large, improvements are uniform in style and architecture and are well maintained, population is of the substantial type and popularity of the area is indicated by the volume of new construction in past two years.     Jump in grade, from first to third for area just south, is explained by the fact that there is a strip of vacant territory about 2 blocks wide between the two areas and the property fronting on Tazewell Road is adversely affected by encroaching business, filling stations, etc.
Low income wage earners of various kinds

This is an area about 25% improved, lying outside city limits. Terrain is rolling. Improvements are of very cheap construction and maintenance is only fair. Has all utilities except public sewerage and some of the homes have outside toilets - others septic tanks.     Along Tazewell Road on the north side of the area are several stores, filling stations, etc., and the few homes located on this Road are much better than those in the southern part of the area. Cemetery is located adjoining on the east by apparently does not adversely affect this area.     Transportation is by gasoline bus along Tazewell Road and Jacksboro Pike and schedules are adequate. Grade school located in adjoining areas to north and large county high school in area C-8, within walking distance.     Cheap construction, unfavorable appearance and type of population make this a third grade area.
Business and professional men and executives
Built for lot owners as homes

Between Dickson & Western Ave. South of Church St. are houses ranging in price up to $50,000 averaging $20,000 - those lands are of considerable age but in good condition. Negro is confined to Olive Ave section.

A new subdivision with large, well wooded lots gently rolling terrain, known as "Harrill Hills", about 25% improved. Improvements are uniform in style and architecture and well constructed. Subdivision is well laid out and has charm and appeal.     It is located in Fountain City, an unincorporated village, free from Knoxville city taxes. Has all utilities except public sewerage, each house having its septic tank. Transportation is by gasoline bus along Jacksboro Pike and schedule is adequate. No school in area but both grade and high school in walking distance. Fountain City business center not far distant.     Population is substantial, style and construction uniform and popularity of the area is indicated by volume of new construction in past two years.
Hilly - sloping up from Beaver Road.
Demand from R. R. Workers - good train transportation, street car and bus service, new blvd. into section. More ground around houses.
Strictly residential section. Properties along Roosevelt Blvd. have been built within past 10 years.
Hilly - sloping up from the river - level at eastern end.
Smoke & dirt & fog from river - mill in Neville island south of California gives off silt which blows into this section.
Hilly - rolling territory on top of mound
Very desirable residential with high class populace.
All new construction built for specific individuals.  Large country club located here.  Atmosphere in general very good
Hilly, sloping up from Ohio River, very little level ground.
Good bus service - shopping center; good schools
Smoke, dirt, and fog from river and mills and factories on Neville Island.
Neighborhood has some very large homes now converted to duplexes and rental units. Streets in good condition.
Good transportation - relatively new territory good streets - property well designed and in good condition.
Good on brick - Only fair on frame
Certain portions of Danes Ave. Terman Ave. and Orchlee Avenues contain very fine homes up to $30,000 which have been built in past 18 months. Section is quite active.
Entire area is on high ground sloping on both sides
Good transportation. Near Park. Desirable residential section of modest character.
Spotty bad paving, some streets are steep.
Southern part - average type, white collared & executive type in northern part
The northern section is an exclusive territory. Pride of ownership is very prevalent. Trend of development is due north. Some very good houses along Perrysville Ave. fronting on the Park.
Very hilly, comprised of 4 separate hills and two valleys
Near to business section; transportation fairly good throughout.
Bad odor from disposal plant and stockyards, spotty.
This is a larger territory, people are mortgage conscious in sections of Troy Hill, Spring Hill & Pineview, resulting in few foreclosures.
Low lying territory along Allegheny and Ohio rivers part flood land.
None from standpoint of home ownership.
Dirt, filth, smoke etc. low type community. One of the toughest sections of Pittsburgh.

This is one of the older sections of Pittsburgh which is gradually being taken over for commercial purposes. Some 800 properties are reported condemned by the city. These were damaged by recent flood etc. Generally speaking this section is classed as the lower or undesirable type. Most of property located there can be purchased for ground value.
Fairly level, sloping up from Ohio river.
Some industry located in the sections.
Pride of ownership is evident. Not much change in community.
Good transportation, shopping center, within walking distance downtown Stores and offices. Near employment of diversified character.
Old district. No room for residential expansion. Future commercial.

Land values are holding section up at present in hope of conversion bus. District of Charles & Strauss Sts. is about 40% colored; about 20% undesirable white population. Some very fine homes still occupied by original owners.
Has its own shopping center, good transportation, rather an old community. Good school and high school.
Subject to flood in 28 foot stage; sewer backage in business section.
Relief load heavy in spots; average for community.
Rolling land on top of hill
New development - pleasingly designed building and entire area well kept.
Streets are not paved, but cindered and well kept.
Fairly new residential area of very modest character.
Large reservoir located here. No transportation, Many Unpaved Streets.
This is a poor man's community generally speaking. No building restrictions. Section is somewhat isolated.
All located in valley and hillsides surrounding the valley.
Good transportation; small town within itself; good railroad facilities; good employment center in good times.
Smoke and dirt from steel mills.
Subject to floods - Mills, factories, railroads, smoke, dirt, etc.
Area is subject to floods, old buildings being torn down. Fast becoming commercial and industrial territory. Generally speaking, properties can be purchased for ground value.
Convenient to mills and factories, fair transportation, good schools.
Smoke and dirt from nearby mills, factories, odors from river, subject to high water flood.
A small old town in itself; more depreciation and obsolescence apparent year after year. Territory damaged by 1936 flood.
Good transportation, convenient to employment and shopping center
This is considered a good working man's district with houses of modest character always in good demand. Section lies out of the flooded area.
Good transportation, near employment of diversified nature.
Old homes in poor condition, subject to floods, smoke and noise from mills.

No demand for home purchase since flood. Property near Butler St. between 40th and 47th avenues is considered slightly better than the balance of this section. There is a number of joint home and business properties on  Butler St. Where vacancy is heavy in upstairs units. Many are in vandalized condition. Small industry is sprinkled throughout the area. Mills have moved out of the section and have taken much skilled labor with them.
Hilly, sloping up from Butler Street.
Near parks. Convenient to employment and commercial areas. Good transportation.
Considered a good workingman's district. Buildings are old but substantially built. Diversified employment is nearby.
J. C. McKenna, Griffin & Co. Property Mgmt. Broker
Heavy taxes. Large houses difficult to sell.

This is a high class rooming house section with many large houses having been converted to boarding houses. Land values are helping to hold up prices of properties. There are some old apartments with cheap rents which are attracting a less desirable element.
Good transportation in Southern end. Near employment.
Poor class of small houses in poor condition.
This is a good 4th grade section. Some Polish people built here about 4 yrs. ago along Kincaid.
Bounded on North by good section. Near shopping section. Good transportation.
Negro encroachment threatening. Congested area. Obsolescence.
A mediocre section at East Liberty.
Near Park. Good general character of people and structures.
Most of the rental units are duplexes. New building is on subdivided ground of large estates and older houses.
Good transportation - Public & private schools, local shopping center. Suburban atmosphere
Heavy summer traffic to local amusement park.
Considerable development is taking place due north of this section in a development called Wellington Heights, houses there range up to $40,000.
Very fine high school, good bus transportation, suburban atmosphere.
In northern portion pride of ownership is exceptionally good. Community spirit prevails. Nice quiet section.
Entire area level ground extending back from Allegheny river.
Good transportation, railroad, street car and bus.
Professional and Business & white collared class 40%, Laboring & RR 60%
Commercial section of "Aspinwall" located in this district on First Street.
Mostly level - upgrade in North end
Good employment during mill activity good streets.
Some smoke and dirt from nearby mills.
Professional & business & white collar men, 60%; Mill workers & RR Men, 40%
Newer homes are located in the northern part of this area - price of ownership is evident and properties are generally well maintained.
The area is aristocratic. Pride of ownership is very good.  All construction for specific individuals; no operative building.
Level to hilly in Western end
Near Park. Good transportation. A section of modest homes of good character.

Jewish encroachment at southern end from Bryant to Staunton Sts. between Duffield and Heeth St. Better homes are on Morningside avenue between Wellesley and Bryant. Insurance companies are active in this section.
Level to hilly in Eastern end
Good transportation. Near Park. Desirable residential section. Considered good location.
Singles - duplexes - some rows and apartments

Values have been depressed by Jewish encroachment on the following streets: Jancey St. to North St. Clair between Hays and Wellesley. Activity has increased noticeably in past 12 months. This is a fair second grade section.
Fairly desirable residential area. Well located, near park and Cultural center
Obsolescence, steep ascent, very spotty only fair transportation. Overcrowded.
Many old houses in fairly good condition. This is a poor third grade area.
Level to sloping upward to Centre Ave.
Good location. Good transportation. Near Colleges and cultural centers.
Heavy traffic. Proximity to RR and industrial plants.
Downward as residential except on Lytton, Tennyson and Ruskin Streets
Property here is very high grade in good condition ranging in price up to $40,000, and is not to be considered in the same class as the balance of the area.
Good transportation. Old but well established and desirable residential section. Near Civic center.

One of the few level sections in Pittsburgh. A very stable demand exists for property in this section. Large estates are being broken up and smaller units replacing very large houses. Section is graded first grade because of activity and desirability of the area. Older houses at present are difficult to sell except where demolition is feasible and subdividing of ground profitable.
Highly desirable residential area. Good transportation and shopping center. Good elevation.

One of the best sections in the city limits - Houses from $15,000 to $25,000 predominate. Section is threatened with Jewish encroachment from south. Forbes St. frontage is expected to be zoned for apartments.
Good transportation - good schools, convenient shopping district, close to parks, good elevation.
Slight Jewish encroachment, two new aparts. built off Murray Ave. Considerable commercial Bldg. on Murray Ave. Near Forbs.Very active business center.
Good transportation. Very good public and private schools. Well restricted. Zoned for best development.
About 50% of this section is older houses and 50% fairly new. Very little room for expansion or new building except on divided estates.
Fairly level on top of hill
Fairly new section well located - near park, good elevation
A small section of good character well protected from encroachment.
Good transportation - schools - shopping district, near parks
White collar class - clerks - some professional men
STRONG JEWISH INFLUENCE OF FAIR TO LOWER CLASS JEW.
Near Park and Country Club - good elevation, good transportation, convenient shopping district
Strong Catholic influence in this section
Good transportation, near employment, better class of working men.
The section is holding up very well. Considered a desirable residential area for workers in this area. Not attractive to outsiders.
Sloping up the hill from the river
Good transportation. Near employment, practically no foreign. Good business section.
Few negro in section. Practically a small town within the city.
Property south of Bates avenue is of Better character than those north of this street.
Robert Murray, Asst. to St. Mgr. in charge of sales.
Level, only slightly above river level.
Good transportation. Near employment of diversified nature. Good local business section.

Negro concentrated in the northern end of the area. Most of the row houses are held for investment. Values are not expected to increase but to continue their decline still further. Demand for these cheap rental units has been responsible for the entire area.
Always in demand if local mills operate. Diversified employment nearby.
Very spotty with entire area dependent on local mills which reopened only in early 1936.
Bldg. and loan assns. which normally financed this section are not in position to lend any volume of mortgage money.
M. Colbert - Property Mgmt. Div. HOLC
Similar in character to the other two sections of Ambridge colored red.
Same as D 31, except some newer homes.
Houses very close together, concentration of foreign & negro.

Industry started again in 1936. Building and Loan Assns. had heavy foreclosures throughout. A strictly industrial section attracting only laboring classes. Negro coming in from Leetsdale to get closer to local employment.
Flood hazard yearly to some degree. Poor housing.
Entirely dependent on local mills which only recently reopened.
Near employment which is now active
One principal industry for local support.
Oakmont properties are slightly better than Verona
Suburban atmosphere - desirable residential section. Good transportation to Pittsburgh
Local plants have become active in 1936 after being closed for several years. Old established town again feeling prosperity of mills. Present occupants have been located here for some time.
Flood hazard yearly to some degree. Poor housing.
Entirely dependent on local mills which only recently reopened.
Good employment during mill activity, good roads.
White collared & executive 40%, skilled labor & coal Minors 60%
A few very expensive houses are located in this area. A large number of properties are "Company owned".
Obsolescence. Poor condition of structures, lower class populace.

Land values on Penn. Ave. in E. Liberty between Frankstown & Highland Ave. range from $10,000 to $15,000; it is the shopping center for the entire East End District. Chain stores and mail order houses located here. Larimer Ave. is the shopping center for Italian population. Eastern end of this section is best. No market for row houses. Single houses average $1500-5000, about 60% of the owner-occupied homes are mortgaged.
Heavy obsolescence, surrounded by two poorer areas
A section lying in part between two very poor areas. Depreciation is expected to continue very fast because of this influence. About 60% of the owner-occupied homes are mortgaged.
Near employment in E. Liberty district.
Concentration of foreign and negro. Houses in poor condition.
Many original owners selling on liberal terms in order to get out of the section.
Only fair transportation. Future of this section is very uncertain. Negro encroachment threatening.
A modest development originally intended for small home owner. Foreclosures were heavy in this section. About 60% of the owner occupied homes are mortgaged. A poor third grade section.
Good transportation, old but well established residential area with good business section.
About 50% of the workers are employed in industrial plants and mills along the Manongahela River. The Central part of Wilkinsburg is considered slightly better than the balance of the section.
Fairly new development of uniform and modest character. Suburban atmosphere.
Sales market only improved in past 12 months. Marketability somewhat hampered by poor transportation to some corners of this section. Many Westing house employees live here.
Good train transportation - high class populace
Houses on Maple Avenue range up to 50,000 but the section as a whole is fairly uniform with some moderately large houses. About 60-65% of the owner occupied homes are mortgaged.
Homogeneous development of good character. Fairly good transportation. Section overlooks Frick Park.
None except distance to commercial section.
This is only a fair 1st grade section.
Near employment. Exceptionally good schools. Fairly desirable residential section.

Building prices on new construction has increased about 25% in 12 months of $1200 per unit. Occupants with improved income are anxious to move out. Sales demand is from foreign element in Braddock and Rankin. Local workers dependent on steel mill activity - Shayer Avenue section is the 5th avenue of this area with values ranging up to $15,000. There is a strong church influence in the area.
Sloping up from the river - steeply up from Braddock Ave.
Old houses in poor condition, many houses have no bath, smoke & noise from industry.
A poor section housing workers with limited incomes.
Near employment - very good local shopping center.

There is no room for expansion in the city of Braddock with the result there is a tremendous demand for business as the local steel plants are running under 80% of capacity. Values placed on houses by people living in the area are not commensurated with their real worth, but because of the limited ground available prices on present units remain high. The section between N. Holland Ave, 5th St. from Corey to Holland Ave is the best of the section.
Similar in character to Swissvale except slightly further out from the center of Pittsburgh
Bessemer Terrace to Ridge Ave. Between Grandview Ave. and Western Ave. has property better than the balance of the section.
Sub-Pittsburgh - Part of Forest Hill - No. of E. Pitts.
Homogeneous section modest homes - generally desirable
Developed by Westinghouse for office employees and shop foremen
Near employment - Poor transportation to work.
Concentration of foreign and negro in poor housing
High social Standard - Desirable better class housing. Good train & bus service.
Some of Pittsburgh wealthier people own homes in this section.
Desirable suburban residential section within commuting distance of Pittsburgh.
Section is somewhat spotty but its general character is good.
Property in this area is very well held; few were placed on the market during the depression. Negro employed as domestics.
Low ground - poor houses - concentration of foreign and negro
Standard Steel Spring Co. strike of 4 months settled early in 1937 has held up recovery which will soon come up to other comparable sections nearby.
Near local employment - good shopping district. Suburban atmosphere. Local mills operating.
As is typical of small towns, this entire area is very spotty with good and bad properties intermingled. It is not uncommon to find negro houses adjacent to much better units.
Neighborhood is very spotty. Distance to Pittsburgh.
This section is very spotty with negro scattered through the best parts. Suburban section to the south, although not shown on map, is very good.
Desirable section of smaller houses of somewhat recent date. Good transportation. Local employment.
Most of the residents work locally.
Bottom of valley - sloping up the hillside
Good transportation, local employment, convenient to shopping center.
Section lies poorly, overcrowding of housing.
Arch Street section is particularly bad.
Good transportation, out of noise, near local employment

Section was very bad during the low of the market, but has had definite improvement since 1935. Second generation moving out of the area on Washington, Buckwood and Broadway. Between Ridge and Buckwood for two blocks on each side of Trimble Street are located the best houses in the city ranging in price up to $50,000. Most of the houses are of considerable age, however, with a very limited demand for resale at present these are occupied by local business men and plant executives.
Near employment, values holding up because of possibility of selling to Carnegie Steel Co.
Houses in very poor condition. Smoke and noise from mills
Speculators are taking options on properties in hope that Carnegie will buy. There has been some demolition in the section. One of the few level spots in the vicinity.
Sloping steeply up the hill from Duquesne Road
Near employment. The best residential section of the city. Considered quite desirable.
About 15 houses have been built in 1937 to sell for $3500 to $4500; all for specific individuals. This is a heavily congested area as is most of Duquesne.
Sloping steeply up from Duquesne Road
Smoke and dirt from the steel mills. Poor houses in poor condition.
The only support for the entire Duquesne section is the one Carnegie mill locally.
Sloping steeply up from Duguesne Road
Near employment - fairly desirable residential section with some good houses.
Section is quite spotty. Smoke and Dirt from mills.
Part of the section is outside Duquesne city limits.
More space around houses. Good elevation. Good rental demand.
No paved streets. Sewers partially lacking poor transportation, Heavy taxes, steep ascent from Duquesne.
Static if improvements are put in.
This section will not bring the prices that Duquesne properties will. Section is enjoying overflow of housing demand from Duquesne.
Level on top of hill back of section C.
Away from smoke from steel mill
Poor property - close to slag dump
Edw. H. Fahey - Property Mgmt. Broker
Level on hill top overlooking Manogahela River
Near employment - fairly new and desirable residential well removed from smoke from mills.
A Small section outside Duquesne city limits
There is considerable changing of occupants in this section. Houses on Duquesne Blvd. near Outlook Ave. are very good.
Near employment. Good elevation and well planned development.
Poor transportation. Steep ascent to section.
Entire area dependent on mill activity.
Vacant ground is too hilly for development
Suburban atmosphere. Convenient location near employment and shopping district. Good elevation.
Some unpaved streets. Only fair transportation. Some cheap construction.
Streets east of Ellsworth have no sewers.
Fair transportation. Isolated section of poor houses.
Poor transportation, isolated section of poor houses.
Housing demand from Homestead has overflowed into this section.
Near employment. Good class of people.
J. C. Kuhn - Property Mgmt.t Broker
This is a good 4th grade section. Entire area depends on mill activity.
Near employment, near park and library. Good class of populace.
Many mill superintendents and better paid office employees live here.
Level - sloping slightly up from the river
Near employment - convenient to shopping district on 8th Ave.
Smoke from steel mills. Houses are overcrowded, mixture of population.

Many houses have two and three families living in two or three rooms. Rents were not collectable when mills were shut down. Considerable demolition 1933-35 to save taxes. Good possibility of ground between river and RR being purchased by industry. Property south of 8th Avenue is slightly better.
Good elevation overlooking river, near employment suburban atmosphere.
Section is very spotty, cheap construction, no sewers or paving in some parts.
Valley section marked Hays is very crowded
Fairly new desirable residential area with suburban atmosphere. Good bus service.
None except distance to commercial area
Activity only started in past 15 months. Principally F.H.A financing on new construction.
Gerald A. Born, Property Management Broker
Rolling - slopes down from Brownesville Road which is the crest of the hill.
Good bus transportation - rather desirable residential section.
30 units built in 1937 to sell from $7,000-10,000. A fairly good section usable for expansion from Knoxville, Carrick & Mt. Oliver.
Hilly, sloping both sides from Brownesville road
White collar class - clerks - small business men

Knoxville is a very stable neighborhood - houses are better than most of the rest of the section but the entire area is very spotty. Many houses need paint and minor repairs. About 55% of the owner occupied homes are mortgaged.
Surrounding territory is good and new development appears to be better in this section.
None except topography, some question of undermining
The least developed section which is close to the commercial area of Pittsburgh.
Good transportation, bus trolley - Desirable residential area. Restricted development.
Much of the territory is undermined and some houses have sagged slightly.

Dormont has a very good business section, a post office branch and two branch banks. Brookline also has a branch bank and a shopping center on Brookline Blvd. Greatest danger of mine cave is in lower lying section.
J. C. Gilson - Property Mgmt. Broker - Freehold Realty Co.
Hilly, sloping up from W. Liberty Road.
Direct transportation through tubes to Pittsburgh business district.
Houses on small lots not well planned
Strong Catholic influence in this area. Advance in rentals must be predicted on reconditioning.
Hilly - sloping down from Brownesville Road, section
Many unpaved streets. Topography is not readily appreciable to residential building. Section is very spotty with much cheap construction of considerable age.

Mortgage funds are available at 40-50% of appraisal. A good portion of these properties are built on the hillside and valley bottoms. Negro concentrated in St. Clair. Section is very spotty throughout. Many houses need paint and minor repairs.
Level to hilly - sloping up from river.
Very poor neighborhood - smoke and soot from mills - flood area.

A very spotty section with some fair property on some streets. Some demolition for reducing taxes. Most of this section lies at the foot of the hill along the Monogahela river. About 45% of the owner-occupied homes are mortgaged. All alleys built with rows. 17th to 22nd on Sarah, Jane, & Mary are good class Polish. German settlement on St. Pauls off South 18th St.
Good transportation, near employment, good elevation
Heavy obsolescence, houses too close together
Thrifty class of people in this locality many old German families. Houses in the Buell foundation section are definitely better than the rest of the section; Oneida St. south of Virginia.
Homogeneous development of good character. Good transportation. Very desirable residential section.
Some danger of mine cave causing houses to sag, particularly on the hill sides.

Recent letting of contract to pave Banksville Road will add another outlet for heavy traffic into this area. The foreclosures were very heavy throughout Mt. Lebanon. About 80 % of the homes were mortgaged in 1934.
Fairly new residential area surrounded by good sections. Good Transportation.
Dust from Coal mine. Undermining of ground. No sewers on Southern hills edge
Coal operations have stayed development of this section.
W.S. Klemons - Property Appraiser, HOLC Pittsburgh
Near center of town - near Civic center Park
Concentration of negro and undesirables, very congested.

Considerable Jewish throughout the 5th Ave. Section. Demolition for tax purposes and poor condition. Values of residential structures is expected to continue down. Rentals have about reached a peak now. Northeast corner is the best of the entire section: North of Webster and East of Morgan. The poorest area in the territory bounded by 5th Ave., Congress St., Bedford & Erin St. has been mentioned for slum clearance.
Good transportation. Very convenient location. Good class of populace.
Age of many properties. Possibility of apartment house encroachment.

A rather old section but it is well established. About 55% of the owner-occupied homes are mortgaged. A fair second grade section. Hastings Avenue as far south as Rockshale Road has poorer housing in only fair condition.
Considered a desirable residential section. A wooded section of good character. Good populace.

Older houses not finding a ready market, but new homes are being built for specific individuals. Only about 200 houses in this section. Section east of Park Road is not up to the standard of the balance of Rosslyn Farms area.
Hilly, rolling down from hill top

Crafton has larger ground units and the section enjoys a good name, although part of the area is spotty. Many original owners still in the section, but younger generation is not       locally.  Properties on hill tops are generally considered more desirable than than those on hillside.
Obsolescence setting in in parts of the area, slowly going foreign.
Lorenz Ave. to Chartier Ave. are business. Strahle Place houses are good and fairly new ranging in price up to $9000. Ordinary section of modest homes.
Near employment of well diversified character.

Little demand for housing since the 1936 flood - values are not expected to improve from the present low level. Rents have increased as rapidly as other section because of uncertainty of receivership of Pressed Steel Car Co.
Hilly, in a valley between hills
Near employment, fairly desirable residential area for better paid local workers.
Mixture of older houses in fair condition
Outside city limits of McKees Rocks. Good demand for units from workers locally. RR shops, many industries located nearby.
Lies in bottom of valley - sloping up from river.
Old property in poor condition, concentration of negro & foreigners.

Demolition in the section. Developing into light manufacturing. Main St. is commercial. Many slum houses held for income purposes. Other houses are not expected to increase over present valuations. most of the dwelling units are overcrowded.
Homogeneous development of high class homes. Wooded section of newer homes attracting younger local business. Good transportation.
This is the newest development in the city. Sales prices increased only in early 1937. The foreign which has bought into this area is of very high class and not undesirable to other residents.
Rolling to level at Northern end.
Good transportation- schools-churches. Desirable residential of homogeneous development.
Considered a good residential area. Commercial area centered at Norwood and Highland Avenue. Before the development of A-1 and A-2 this section was the best residential section of New Castle.
Slightly rolling toward center of city.
Restricted development of high class homes. Good Transportation.

Previous to developments of section A-1 this area was the very best residential section in the city. It is still very desirable with high class populace residing in original homes. As is typical of smaller towns, some streets are a little spotty, but the reputation of the section is good.
Fairly new desirable section with good transportation. Convenient to center of city.
Growth is anticipated because of general desirability of the area. The section is a modest development of smaller homes of good character.
Good transportation- schools, churches. Desirable residential area of modest homes.
Commercial area centered at Wellington and Edison Avenues.
Sloping slightly toward center of city.

Many original owners still living in the section. Some large houses are being converted into apartments. Section is slowly going into business and is in direct line of growth; expansion however, will be very slow. Originally the best section of New Castle.
Level - steeply up the hill in Western end.
A boarding & rooming house section of only fair character.
None except free from industrial dirt.
Removal of local employment - poor houses - Distance to center of city.
A large cement plant which formerly furnished employment to workers is this section closed down during the depression and its reopening is questionable. There are few paved streets in this area.
Level close to center of city. Sloping in eastern end.
Housing here is in fair demand because the section is fairly clean and away from the industrial plants along the river.
Good transportation. Several parks in the area.
Commercial section along South Mill St. and at Pearson & Taylor. Shopping center on Long St.
Some unpaved streets - heavy foreign population.
Foreign from this section trying to move into B-4. The area in return is attracting residents from section C-5.
Good transportation - schools - churches. Desirable section of modest homes.
Section is attracting better class of foreigners from south side. Washington Street has small business throughout its entire length.
Near employment and local shopping center. Large hospital keeps hospital attendants locally.
Smoke & noise from mills - class of population.
Negro and white intermingled in poor housing which is in demand when local mills are operating as they now are.
New Castle & So. New Castle Penn.
Near employment along river. Four shopping center. Has own Polish schools and churches.
No sewers outside city limits. Smoke & soot from mills.
Section is known as Goat Hill. Considered a very stable neighborhood with good type Polish inhabitants.
Smoke, dirt and noise from mills. Low class populace. Poor houses.

Very poor section located between two industrial plants which make the area very dirty. Many shack type houses scattered throughout and the section is desirable primarily because it is near employment.
Dirt and noise from mills. Obsolescence. Housing in poor condition. Low class populace.

Greatest value is for conversion to business purposes. Commercial growth of the city is in opposite direction. This section is similar in character to D-3 but not as well located for business expansion. Rentals were not collectable during depression and vacancy was the heaviest in the city.
Many apts. not fit for use.

Greatest value of property is for conversion to business but growth of the commercial area is in the opposite direction. There is a good percentage of apartments above business properties. Rentals during depression were difficult to collect and vandalism was prevalent.
Concentration of negro in poor housing. Many houses are too low for sewer line.
Labor - low class white and negro
A very poor negro section known locally as Snake's Rest.
A poor section of lower class inhabitants living in crowded quarters.
Good elevation - good transportation. Somewhat isolated from dirt from industrial plants.
No city sewers in some parts.
Low taxes - good schools. Quiet residential section of good character.

This location is very good and activity is expected to continue. Many lots have been sold recently. Development will probably be of modest homes on fairly good sized lots. Financing is available on somewhat limited terms.
Level to hilly in northern end.
Principally a mill section depending on industrial activity of mills.
Two good streets of desirable properties near R.R. employment.
Smoke and noise from mills & R.R. yards.
Through trains of P. & L.E. R.R., & O. and Pa. R.R. run through this town making bus contact with New Castle. This is the best residential part of Mahoning.
Smoke, dirt and noise from mills. Low class populace. Poor houses.
Similar in general character to Section D-7.
Smoke, noise and dirt from mills. Subject to flood in part.
An industrial laborers section of poor housing in good demand primarily because of location and cheap rentals.
Cindered streets. Bus transportation. Near Inverness Golf Course. Proximity to most highly restricted residential areas (A 1, 2 & 3).
Limited utilities. Distance to schools, churches and stores. Restrictions only fair. Spotty repair of homes. Dead end streets. Outlying.

Area should show better activity with return of business conditions, due to surroundings. More intense development, however, will be retarded because of limited utilities and distance to churches, schools and community center.
Unplatted surrounding areas. Small isolated plant. Limited utilities.
A few high priced homes on Overlook Boulevard. Much cheaper in south section of area. Trend is static. Too small an addition to attract much attention.
Outlying district adjacent to farmland. Poor demand. Will probably see low price values in new building construction.
Cindered roads. Transportation. Near Scott Park and Toledo University.
Poorly restricted district. Might improve with increased employment because of proximity to industry.
Unpaved streets, narrow lots. Proximity to railroad, industrial and cemetery.
Fairly clean as Class "D" areas go. Poor class of residents. No demand for sale.
Streets, transportation, churches and schools, utilities.
Encroachment of commercial and industrial. Traffic noise.

Area is 45% industrial and commercial. Trend is downward. Detroit Avenue is gradually becoming a business street. Dorr Street is 100% commercial already. Nebraska Avenue is about 25% commercial. Comprises the west end, Polish district and old middle class residential sections. Negro encroachment is threatening on the east side of area.
Proximity to business district and few industries.

A cheap run down neighborhood, generally. A Government tenancy project was completed last month. Occupants are all colored. Area surrounding project, however, is bad. Large number of houses being demolished by owners and otherwise.
Cheap run-down community rapidly transcending to light industrial and commercial occupancy. Oldest slum district in town.
Zoned light industrial. A few fairly decent homes left in entire area. On whole it is least desirable of any area in town, from a residential standpoint.
Transportation, streets, school and churches. Surrounds Art Museum.
Transcending from a good residential district to a lower income class, boarding and rooming houses.
One of the older areas. Slowly being transformed into commercial district along Detroit Avenue. Trend is downward.
Streets, transportation, trees, near schools and churches.
Old aristocratic residential section changing to a good middle class of occupancy. Majority of houses are over-built for present day use. Trend is static.
Old residential district. Lower wage earning occupancy. All large old style over-built homes. Will probably decline in value due to hold style homes.
Streets, trees, transportation, schools and churches. Near shopping center.
Executives and professional and business men

Surrounded by a much lower class of buildings. Main Street (Cherry Street) is zoned "Commercial". The area is fenced in. Was a high class residential section at one time but business and lower class building encroachments tend to pull it down.
Paved streets. Close to downtown district, school, and churches. Transportation.
Borders on "Red" area. Congested and old.
The area is zoned 35 per cent commercial and industrial and the trend is downward. One of the oldest sections close in to town.
Streets, transportation, near schools, churches and community center. Adjoins park.
This area includes the new Polish district within the old Polish settlement. Most employees were formerly with Willys-Overload. Now working part time only or out of employment.
Close to industry. Some, dirt, etc.
This area on the edge of a built up section. Built up with a miscellaneous assortment of homes and scattered groups.
Some better homes in the vicinity of Stickney. Suffers from smoke and dirt from prevailing winds.
Good streets; near churches, schools and business center. Transportation. Accessible to recreation and amusement.

Area lies south of Jermain Park. Popular priced location. Restricted somewhat less than areas A1 to 4, but very clean and pride of ownership is highly evident. Good, sound construction. Within short distance to beautiful Ottawa Park and new University of Toledo.
Streets, transportation, near schools and churches. Adjoins "Green" area on west.
Borders on "Yellow" on south and east. Overlooks industrial center on the north.

Attempt to make a high priced addition of this area was unsuccessful, Few high priced homes were built some 15 years ago. Poor appeal on account of industrial and lower priced area surrounding. Will probably see lower priced construction.
Good streets and transportation; convenient to churches, schools and community market. Accessible to recreation and amusement. Within very short distance to University of Toledo.
Encroachment of industry and lower grade area (C-18) on the east.

Located immediately south of Ottawa and Jermain Parks. Still fairly desirable. Better homes in the north and west section of area. Properties on east side suffer what due to presence of industry nearby.
Good streets, trees, near schools and churches, good transportation. Adjoins park.
Restricted to single residences. A little older but a very fine and high type neighborhood. Trend is upward. A few very expensive homes.
Transportation; good streets; convenient to churches, schools, University and markets.
Abutts cemetery on the west and Yellow area (C-18) on east and south sides.

A somewhat older but very fine, high type neighborhood. Pride of ownership is highly evident. Area was well planned and homes soundly constructed. Uniform and stable population. Within short distance to University of Toledo. Abutment to cemetery and lower grade area should not jeopardize desirability for several years.
Streets, utilities, near schools and churches.
Adjoins cemetery on east and on the south by cemetery and cheaper area. On west by industrial.
Located sufficiently close to park and Toledo University grounds to hold its own for several years. Activity is slow however.
Good streets, near churches and schools, adjoins beautiful.
Borders on cemetery and railroad track.
Some duplexes along Greenway and Kensington Drive. Clean neighborhood. Upward trend.
Streets. All utilities. Very clean, high grade neighborhood.
The second best residential neighborhood. Very fine and clean lots well landscaped. Trend is upward.
Part of Ottawa Hills and Old Orchard
Close to schools, paved streets, high class residential. Fully restricted and zoned Class "A".
The highest class residential district. Well restricted Pride of ownership is highly evident. Trend is upward. West of city limits.
Trees, paved streets, all conveniences, scenic; high restrictions.
This is the finest and most expensive residential district. Very beautiful estates. The "cream" of better residential districts. Located in village of Ottawa Hills, west of Toledo city limits.
Abutts high class Green (A-3) area. Good roads; convenient to churches, schools and markets. Bus transportation.

Area is fairly well built up except for north section. Good, clean and desirable location small tradesmen and mechanics. Somewhat lower restrictions but the demand should continue due to area being located next to the most expensive and most highly restricted residential community (Areas A-1, 2 & 3)
Streets, transportation, near schools and churches.
Somewhat cheaper homes along railroad track. Rather mixed district of bungalows and 1 1/2 story homes. Not far from industry. Should improve with employment situation.
Good streets, transportation. Near schools and churches.
It is a good popular priced location. Clean neighborhood. Restrictions are somewhat lower than in Areas A-1 and 4. Should continue to show upward trend.
Paved streets. Transportation. Surrounds Devilbiss High School and Campus and Bounded on all sides by "B" areas.
Lots are 30 feet. Homes are crowded. Good rental district because of proximity to large industries.
Good streets, clean neighborhood. Zoned Class "A" residential, Church, school, transportation and trading center conveniently available. Accessible to recreation and amusement.

Area lies north Jermain and Ottawa public parks. Ottawa park is beautifully wooded. Very high class residential section. Within walking distance to the new University of Toledo. Construction is sound and the area was well planned.
Good streets, clean neighborhood, zoned Class "A" residential. Near schools and churches.
It is the best class medium priced residential district. Well restricted. Trend is upward. Occupied by the younger element of professional and high salaried men.
Transportation, near schools and churches, streets.
Beyond city limits. Good community. Eventually should be taken into city. Street paving program now in effect, should stabilize values in this section.
No other utilities. Outlying section. Surrounded by unplatted areas on three sides. Poorly restricted.
Addition has never developed to any extent and any improvements will consist of cheaper priced homes.
Streets, transportation. Near schools and churches. Close to business center. Adjoins park.
Adjacent to cemetery on south and Sylvania Avenue which is zoned "commercial."
One of the older well established and built up residential district and within walking distance of Toledo's largest industrial center.
Transportation. Streets. Schools and churches. Close to industry.
Encroachment of industry on the south.
Better and cleaner homes north of Sylvania Avenue. District south of Sylvania Avenue is somewhat blighted by encroachment of industry and cheaper wage earners.
Slow in developing and surrounded by unplatted areas.
Grading of streets neglected. Many dead-end streets. Somewhat isolated. Laid out during boom of Willys-Overland Plant.
Trees, wooded section in parts of area.
Cindered roads, outlying section. Sparsely built up. Poorly restricted. No utilities excepting electricity.
Too far out and absence of utilities are a deterrent to sales activity. Mortgage lending is very limited. Unattractive and surrounded by unplatted lands.
Cindered street; electricity available in area. Within fair distance to industry.
Outlying. No utilities with exception of electricity; surrounded by unplatted areas on 3 sides. Poorly restricted. Considerable distance to schools, churches and shopping district.

Addition has never developed to any extent and improvements will consist of cheaper priced homes. Lack of adequate utilities, poor transportation and outlying location will result in influx of lower income groups, in the future.
Area has electricity and water. Fair distance to Industry in north end of city. Clean neighborhood.
Surrounded by unplatted areas; limited utilities. Poor streets; lack of adequate transportation; somewhat isolated. Dead end streets. Heavy traffic on Detroit Ave.

Area consists of single frame homes; fairly restricted. Laid out along with other sections some 15 years ago with the expansion of North-end development of the city. Improvements will be slow due to outlying location and lack of adequate utilities and transportation.

Outlying. Poor transportation; considerable distance to schools, churches and stores. No utilities excepting Electricity. Poorly restricted; surrounded completely by unplatted areas. Dead end streets.

Area is located just south of the Michigan State boundary. Too far out and completely isolated. Lack of adequate fire and police protection. Built up only 5 percent. Any further improvements will undoubtedly consist of cheaper priced homes and occupancy by lower income groups.
Cindered roads. Has water, sewer, and electricity.
Too far out for better activity at present. Will probably remain "as is" for some years.
No restrictions. No waster, gas, or sewer. Isolated. Surrounded by unplatted lands.
Dead-end streets. Occupied laborers and industrial workers. Little improvement is expected in coming years. Will probably go on the down grade.
Originally platted for summer resort purposes. Has developed into permanent home sites occupied by industrial workers employed in the adjoining oil refineries, glass plant, and coal loading docks.
Paved streets. All utilities. Transport. Near schools and churches.
Originally was the best residential district overlooking the river. Transcended to industrial and rooming house district. Zoned Class "B" residential and industrial.
Good transportation; streets; Convenient to schools, churches and shopping district; adjoins Bay View Park recreation and amusement. Scenic features.
Poor maintenance; influx of colored population and low income group whites.
Area lies in north-east outskirts of city. Formerly a white neighborhood; now rapidly being run down through influx of colored and low income group of whites. Heavy relief load. High vacancy ratio.
Paved streets. All utilities. Near schools and churches. Transportation.
Zoned heavy industrial from Webb Street northeast. Railroads, smoke, dirt, and general obsolescence.

Section lying south-west of Hocking Valley railroad is zoned residential, with the exception of Front Street which is commercial. Definitely downward. Sprinkled with blast furnaces, power plant, and refineries.
Some paved streets. No utilities excepting electricity.
Dead-end streets. Isolated and outlying addition

Very few homes in this area. Two (2) streets are being paved by W.P.A. grants. Not certain whether above project will create any improvement in activity on account of lack of all public utilities and outlying location. A poor third grade area.
This is a newer development on the east side of the city. Slow in building. Improvements consists of well designed modern 6 room houses. Considered the best residential section in East Toledo.
Twenty-five (25) per cent paved streets. Near schools and churches. Adjoins fine park. Adjoins "blue" area.
Seventy-five (75) per cent cindered streets. Poor transportation. Limited utilities. Railroad.
Scattered homes throughout area. Outlying district. Bordered on east by unplatted farm land. Will probably remain static.
Paved streets. All utilities. Close to schools and churches. Transportation. Near business center.
Old residential section in the west half of area. Smoke, dirt, and noise from railroad.
Business men, industrial skilled mechanics, white collared
Somewhat newer homes in the east half of area. Intermingling of old and new houses. Commercial and industrial activities.
