Lack of improvements including paved streets -- no water, sewers -- poor transportation -- no restrictions -- distance from school.

This area of scattered houses is that type of section where a prospective home owner will buy a lot, second hand lumber and build the house himself. It was developed in 1927 - 1929. Of the houses built in the section during the last 14 months, most of them were small and cheaply constructed.
WEST ALLIS & TOWN OF GREENFIELD, WIS.
This area is located in the Town of Greenfield, an area of cheaper houses. That section west of 116th Street, north of Greenfield Park, has the best possibilities in the area.
No sewerage facilities -- tar plant and fertilizer odors.

United States Glue Factory is located here, but is shutting down throwing 450 to 500 men out of employment. The Newport Chemical Company (Dupont Company) is gradually moving away. They own considerable residential property for their employees. Odors from the Chemical plant are very obnoxious. High and Elm Streets and Fifth Avenue to American from north of Elm has water, gas, and electricity. U.S. Glue Company owns many homes for employee and keep them up fairly well. The Flynn Subdivision to the west is a somewhat newer development. No one would live in Carrollville by preference. Anyone who can, will live in South Milwaukee instead. The outlook for the future is discouraging.
Near employment. Out of flood area.
Some smoke and dirt from mill. Many unpaved streets.
Financing is being done by seller. The neighborhood is attractive to foreign who want to be near friends in the vicinity. Better prices are obtainable from this type of buyers than other purchasers.
Near employment - good transportation. Fairly stable demand for units. A desirable section of foreign.
Some dirt and smoke from mills. Hodgepodge mixture of architecture and size of houses.

Such demand as exists for properties in this section is from foreign born or of foreign percentage. Prices obtainable from this class of buyers are quoted, but in view of the short duration of their return to steady employment few are yet in a position to meet the down payment requirements for purchase. Rentals charged are in line with the income of the people and commensurate with their ability to pay. This is a fair third grade section.
None. Out of the flood area. Fairly clean.
Isolated section of the very poor houses. Not readily accessible. No transportation.

This is one of the poorest sections in the Johnstown area. No financing is available under the most favorable circumstances. Housing is very poor and the section is desirable only because of cheap cost of living. Many houses have sufficient ground for truck farming.
In flood zone. Subject to smoke and dirt from mills. A very mediocre section.

Although the houses in this section are similar in character to Morrellville properties, the section is not as desirable to the class of people, who want to live near the steel mills, as the other section. Development has, therefore, been very slow and sales demand is poor. Houses are well occupied because of the general shortage of quarters. Houses deeply inundated during the flood, can not be readily financed by local institutions.
Flood area. Poor housing. Dirt and smoke from R.R. and steel mill.

A very poor section of nondescript houses, many without conveniences. Section was badly flooded in 1936. Streets are unpaved in part and the general character of the neighborhood is not good, but there is good demand from foreigners who want to live in the vicinity of friends and close to mills.
No transportation - smoke and dirt from mills. Partially flooded in 1936.

A very small section isolated without transportation. Properties are built on steep hillside and are very poor. Values were never very high and shrinkage was as severe as possible in view of depreciation taken prior to 1929. Some original families are still living in section.

A sparsely settled section isolated at the top of the hill. The development is very poor and generally undesirable as a residential section. Approach to the area is very steep. Streets in the section are almost impassable. There are no sidewalks and sewer connections are not available throughout. There are less than 100 houses in this neighborhood.
Fairly clean section. No flood hazard.
Steep ascent into area. No shopping center. Some unpaved streets.

This section is isolated on top of a steep hill which is difficult to ascend in bad weather. Its reputation is only fair, although local residents are loyal to the section. There is not a vacant house in the area and 70 families were doubled up in September, 1937. This is a fair third grade section.
Hilly - steeply up from the river.
Out of the flood area. Some remodeling of houses being done. Near employment at Cambria Steel Co.
Smoke and dirt from Steel Mills. Houses need paint badly. Steep ascent into area. Many unpaved streets. Sidewalks are largely lacking. Many houses have no sewers.
Singles predominate - some doubles and rows

There is little homogeneity of structures, the houses being a general mixture in size and architecture. Area is not desirable in point of health. Acid in fumes from mills is very hard on paint. Houses are concentrated principally near Ebensburg Road.
Desirable section although somewhat old. Inclined plane for pedestrian traffic to commercial area. Out of flood area. Clean section.
Age of property. Changing neighborhood. Steep ascent up Mercher highway.

Many owners in section rent rooms to good tenants, some of which are used for light housekeeping. This is the older section of Westmont but character of the neighborhood is good. Some of the houses are not modern and the section is somewhat spotty. New construction is concentrated at southern end. Cheaper houses are at the northern end.
Highest class residential section of Johnstown. Good schools. Inclined plane for pedestrian traffic. Out of flood area.
Poor street car transportation. Steep ascent to section from down town commercial area.

Some new homes being built for individual order at present. This section is a very high grade neighborhood and its character is the best, but the majority of the houses are larger than the demand is for and they are somewhat old, although in good repair. New construction is concentrated along Wayne Avenue.
Good schools and transportation - fairly new section of good character. Taxes are moderate. No flood hazard.
Steep ascent into section. No shopping center.

Section is attracting buyers from 8th ward. This is the newest development in the Johnstown area, but restrictions are very moderate and the area is rather spotty, although the reputation of the section is good. Financing is available on fair terms. There is no uniformity of architecture or trend in development.
Out of flood area. Clean and not crowded
Many unpaved streets. Somewhat inaccessible in bad weather. Transportation is only fair.

Western end of the area is inconvenient to schools. New construction is expected to improve the general desirability of the neighborhood but the contour of the ground is not conducive to high grade development.
Level to rolling - hilly at southern end.
Out of flooded area. Considered desirable section of fairly new houses. Good transportation. No flood hazard.
Nominal except somewhat inaccessible in bad weather.

Substantially built houses on fair sized lots in good condition. Good middle class section. Many local residents would not consider moving out of this section under any circumstances. Because of the lack of building restrictions some streets are spotty, but as a whole the area enjoys a good reputation.
Steep ascent into section - unpaved streets - no sidewalks.
Static - will improve if streets are paved.

Section was just recently taken into the city. Improvements from this association may improve desirability of the area. This neighborhood is surrounded by a good section, but it is somewhat isolated on top of a hill.
Sales demand has never been very good in this section. Some business in section along Valley Pike. Section was badly flooded in 1936.
Desirable residential of modest character. Good transportation. Out of flood hazard.
Skilled labor - middle class - white collar
Similar in general character to Moxham section B-5, although better elevation in this section precludes it from any possible flood danger.
Good transportation and schools. Near employment.
Light industry coming into section along Moxham Ave. Westinghouse building factory between Ferndale & Moxham Avenues near Station St.
Near employment at Lorain Steel Mill. Good transportation.
Flood area. Smoke and dirt from Lorain Steel Mill.

Small business along Central Ave. from Dupont Place to Village Street. There is a possibility that Coleman Street may be zoned for business. The Traction Co. car barn is located on Central Ave. near Bond St.
Good residential neighborhood of modest character. Good transportation. Near steel mill. Out of flood.
Nominal other than lack of uniformity of architecture.

Section has good character with good schools. Houses are substantially built and well maintained although the area is somewhat spotty. This is a desirable middle class section which is attractive to people who have lived in the Moxham area.

An outgrowth of B-5 in Moxham which was developed with only fair housing. Section becomes poorer, as it goes up the hill. Some fair homes on Russell Avenue. Section is very spotty as is Moxham (B-5) but generally speaking the character of the neighborhood is fairly good.
Good transportation. Out of the flood zone above Pine St. Fair section of modest homes.
The portions of this section adjacent to area D-13 are not as desirable as the balance of the neighborhood.
Good schools and transportation. Out of flood area. Desirable section of modest homes in good demand.
Small business men Clerks - skilled labor
Not in Johnstown city limits, although surrounded by the city. This area enjoys a good reputation but the housing warrants only a good third rate grading.
Good transportation. Out of flood area. Good schools. Stable population.
Nominal other than for rather mediocre housing. Topography is not good for high class buildings.
Singles up to $3,500 Doubles up to $5,000

An outlying section of mediocre houses. The area is not popular because of its location. Part of the section is in Dale Boro, an area not in Johnstown city limits, although surrounded by the city. Potential buyers for this class of property are not able generally to meet financing terms at present.
Within walking distance of commercial area.
Walking distance of center of city
Lower end in flooded area. Heavy traffic on Bedford and Horner Streets.
Section has considerable small business located along Bedford Streets with living quarters on second floor.
Near employment - central location. Catholic church and school in area.
Hilly topography. Mixed population. Section has poor reputation.
Negro concentration at lower end. Rents will be raised principally because of location near employment and center of city. Section is reported unsafe at night.
Most of the houses are very old and without some conveniences. Very heavy traffic on Millcreak Road from Westmont and Southmont.
Mediocre neighborhood with many alley houses on limited ground.

Houses backing up to the river are very poor. There is very heavy traffic through the section as the main road to Southmont and Westmont passes through the area as well as the heavy traffic out Franklin St. There has been some vandalism, also. There are 127 families doubled up in the section. Negro concentrated at Western end of this area.
Overcrowded. Badly flooded in 1936. Dirt and smoke from R.R. and Steel mills. Noisy.
Tenements - rows - combined homes and stores

There has not been any transfer in this section for sometime. Property is held primarily for income purposes. Small stores and salons located along Iron St. Low class Jews in the section constitute about 40% of the population. There is a Jewish Synagogue in the section.
Central location. Always in demand on rentals. Some conversion possibly for business use.

In spite of the flood hazard, demand for housing in this section is the best in Johnstown. Top rentals are always charged because of its central location. Many residents rent rooms and some structures have been converted into apartments. There is much small business scattered throughout. Growth of the commercial area is Northwest on Main Street. Doctors’ offices and several clubs are already occupying some of the larger houses. Because of its location in the flooded area mortgage financing is very conservative and values were depreciated severely.
Poor transportation - automobile necessary to commute to work. Many unpaved streets.
An isolated section of fair houses. Area has never been well received because of its location. There is some question as to the class of properties with which the section will develop.
Isolated. No transportation. No sewers. No city water. Very steep ascent.
This section is a German development with no outside sales demand. Sewers are lacking in part. Properties are largely owned by families which have lived in the neighborhood for years.
Isolated on top of hill. Poor transportation.
A sparsely settled section of very poor houses isolated on top of a hill overlooking the R.R. yards and steel mill.
Smoke and dirt from R.R. yards and steel mills. Concentration of lower class populace.

Many small houses in alleys. Houses on hillside are in slightly better condition than those at the foot of the hill, but they are generally less desirable because of location. Originally developed as R.R. Town and is now freight division for Pa. R.R. This is a good 4th grade section.
Low taxes - near employment at steel mills and R.R. yards. Excellent school system. Steel Co. carries tax load.
Smoke and dirt from industry. Houses in very poor condition. Some unpaved streets not passable except on foot.

Most of the houses are concentrated in the first two blocks off Main Street. Bethlehem Steel Co. pays about 80% of the taxes for the operation of this Boro. Main Street is predominately business with dwelling units above stores. Real estate men do not operate extensively here. Many houses in the section are very inaccessible. Houses need paint very badly.
Land rises slightly from the river and becomes rolling and wooded in parts.
Fair accessibility to places of employment
Near aviation field with noise from tasting motors. Also near railroad yards with subsequent dirt and smoke.

A somewhat older section of workingmen's homes where doubles and singles predominate, save south of Brewer Street where only one family homes are found.  Dwellings are similar and not overly attractive architecture, are located on fair sized plots but evidence only spotty pride of ownership. Near the aviation field there is a twenty-four hour din from the testing of motors and in the north constant smoke from the railroad yards. As a whole, the area rates a low "yellow"
In two western portions, danger of flooding is acute is times of very high water.
White collar and small business men

Three fairly new and similar areas containing modest sized homes of somewhat varied architecture. Plots are in proportion, well maintained and generally evidence pride of ownership. The two western sections are subject to floods but only during periods of unusually high water.
In the west land is very low. In the east, it is flat and higher.
Subject to floods in west and smoke and dirt from railroads in the east.

The three sections bordering the river are regularly subject to floods each year which the inhabitants seems to like for it fertilizes their small gardens. In the northeastern section there is no danger from the floods but the area sufferes from soot from the railroad yards. Dwellings throughout the area include everything from shacks to two-family and an occasionally triple. All are in poor condition and evidence no pride of ownernship. The entire area is shunned by lenders and many be classed as "hazardous".
Lack of all improvements and distance from schools , churches, stores, etc.

A small, new and, as yet, sparsely  developed section containing not over 8 or 10 well built and attractively designed homes. Lots are of fair size, well landscaped and evidence a marked pride of ownership. This is the most desirable area for those who must reside in East Hartford
School in area. Stores close. Uniformity of construction. New subdivision. Adequate bus transportation.
Distance to principal business center. Railroad track on Northeast line. Small industrial plants across railroad on Northeast
Aside from the older houses this area is being improved uniformly. Majority of structures conforming with F. H. A. specifications.
Bus transportation adequate. Business center in area. Lake on northwest side. Has all public utilities.
Some distance to school. Part south and southwest side and southeast side not in city limits. Several industrial plants along Denton Drive. Municipal Airport in center of area. Unpaved streets.

About 30 new houses built within past 12 months in Northern part of area between Love Field Drive and Bachman's Lake, along Wylie Drive, Noyes, Weiss and Reeves, and Shore Crest Drive. Also some new building of small houses West of Denton Drive. Southeast part of area contains many smaller houses occupied by factory workers. Airport is being extended toward southeast and it is anticipated that streets will be closed for two or three blocks in this direction, but not many houses to be razed and all only small cheap places.
Attractive design of subdivision - large lots - attractive contour. All city conveniences. Fair building restrictions.
Outside city limits. Some distance to stores and school but bus pickup for school children. Transportation inadequate.
Clerical, business and professional men merchants

A subdivision platted several years ago that experienced rapid growth for a short time only, retarded due to distance from center of city and economic conditions. it is attractively designed containing many lots of natural beauty. Very little rental property in the area.
Schools and stores in area, city conveniences.
Inadequate transportation. Distance to principal business center. Unpaved streets. Mixed construction. Large Cocao Cola plant being constructed adjoining area on south.

An area occupied exclusively by negroes with vacant property on all sides. New plant of Coca Cola Bottling Company being constructed adjoining on south. Very little likelihood of any chance in the area in the near future.
All city conveniences, schools, churches and stores in area. Adequate transportation.
Railroad track, encroachment of small industrial plants, unpaved streets and general mixture of construction. City hospital in area.
Laborers, mechanics, clerical, small merchants, some professional men, etc.

Part of area southeast of St. L. & S.W. R.R. and extreme northeast corner best part of area. Part along railroad tracks and west of Sylvester St. is worst part. On Maple Ave. at Lucas St. is located Cedar Spring Place, Government low-cost housing project. It contains 181 units, has been open one year and all units are reported occupied. Several large, expensive old homes in southeast corner on Turtle Creek Blvd.
Adequate bus transportation. School in area. All city conveniences. Stores not distant.
Surrounding area. Small Industrial Area on Southwest.
In southeastern part of this area located two or three large, expensive estates valued as high as $65,000. Remainder of area a nice section uniformly designed and with uniform construction.
Grade School, churches, community business center in area. Adequate transportation. All city conveniences.
Many apartment houses and duplexes in the area - age of properties. Some unpaved streets. Several boarding and rooming houses in area. Encroachment of business.
Clerical, business and professional men and skilled mechanics
Prescott, Hawthorne & Herschel best streets. Apartment houses and duplexes scattered throughout area. Cheaper area along southwestern line.
Close to business center. Schools, churches, stores in area. Adequate transportation.
Type of population. Old cheap houses predominate. Encroachment of commercial and industrial establishments.
This area adjoins commercial and industrial section. Almost no sales as properties are being held as future business and industrial sites.
Schools, churches, stores in area. Adequate transportation. All city conveniences. Near principal business district.
Railroad tracks through area, cemetery in area. Mixtures of population and type of construction. Encroachment of commercial and industrial establishments, rooming houses.
Better part of area is southeast corner & northeast corner. A general mixture of most every type of old property and also population. Thomas and State streets best negro streets.
High schools, grade schools, churches, stores in area. Adequate transportation. All city conveniences. Park in area.
Railroad tracks through part of area. Old properties. 2 Industrial plants - many large apartment houses of varying degrees of desirability. No restrictions except zoning.
Laborers, clerical, professional and business men

Better apartments on N. Fitzhugh,Ross, Bryan, Live Oak, Mosher, Bennett, Garrett & Trement. Older apartments on Carroll, Annex, Ashby & Peak. Best cottage area on Henderson, Garrett, Belmont, Milam & Alcott. Larger 2 story houses scattered. On N. Fitzhugh, across from Mission, an apartment project of 96 units consisting of about 12 seperate buildings, financed by FHA insured mortgage, has just been completed and opened for occupancy this year.
Uniformity of construction. Adequate transportation. All city conveniences. Grade schools not far distant. Golf course on east.
Western portion contains many structures becoming obsolete on account of age.
Static to upward in eastern part.

West of Greenville is older part except in Northern border, which is new. Eastern part of area has had much activity in new construction during past few years and it is continuing. This entire area is protected by deed restrictions which have several years yet to run. It will continue to be desirable and sales activity will continue to be good in east portion. All land in this area has been platted.
Schools, churches, stores in area. All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Parks in area.
Mixed type of construction - encroachment of commercial and industrial establishments.
Clerical, professional,small merchants, skilled mechanics, etc.
On Garland, Perry, Gurley, Ash Lane, Terry for about 3 blocks on each side of Fitzhugh is better part of area. Southeastern and southern portion worst part of area.
All city conveniences. Park joins on North. Western part of area has adequate transportation and fairly convenient to stores and schools.
Inadequate transportation in Eastern part as street car line stops at Beeman Ave. Schools not very close - Community business on East Grand which is some distance from Eastern part of area.
Just a fair area, mixed type of construction, lower grade area bordering on South and West and undeveloped land in East.
Close to business center. Schools, churches, stores in area. All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Small park in area.
Encroachment of commercial and industrial establishments, junk yards and second hand auto parts stores. Cheaply constructed houses. Type of population.
Laborers, factory workers, clerical, small business men
Singles-8/12 rs. and includes duplexed and some few apt. units
The entire area is a transition from residential to industrial, commercial and apartment houses. As a residential area the portion the greatest distance from the business center is the better part.
Park in area, schools, churches and stores. Close to business center. All city conveniences. Adequate transportation.
Encroachment of commercial and industrial establishments. Railroad tracks through area. Mixed type of population and construction.
Singles 8/12 rs. & includes large old houses made into duplexes
Portion of area surrounding city park is best part of area. Negro population in northeastern part and southern tip. Harwood Park Row, Northeast end of Beaumont, Pocahontas, Gayne are better streets.
High elevation. Golf course joining. New subdivision. Has all city conveniences.
Outside city limits and distance to principal business center. Poor transportation.

This is a new subdivision with only about 20 homes in it. It is owned by one of the large banks in Dallas and is now being pushed by it. It is frequently advertised in in the newspapers, and efforts to create sales demand are meeting with some success due to new construction of modern design and ultra convenient arrangements.
All city conveniences, schools, churches, stores in area. Adequate transportation.
Mixed type of construction and population. Unpaved streets. Cemetery in southeastern part of area.
Clerical, laborers, skilled and unskilled, some small business men.
An area of old houses, not well kept, mixed population, unpaved streets, with practically no outstanding features in its favor.
Schools, stores in area. All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Uniform type of construction.

This area contains a much better type of property than surrounding area, practically all brick and well maintained. Population is largely composed of middle class Jews, and is inclining towards a lower-grade. Ordinarily this would be classed as a 2nd grade area, but due to location, surroundings and tendency to infiltration of lower grade population is is brought down to a high "C".
Schools, churches, and stores in area - has city conveniences. Adequate transportation.
Cheap construction - type of population - unpaved streets. Railroad tracks through area - with some industrial plants located along the tracks.
East end of Spring, Jamacia, Collins, Baldwin, Mckenzie, Fleetwood, Caldwell are best streets. Frazier, Gray, Troy, Italy, Duckett, are worst streets.
Schools and stores in area, has all city conveniences.
Distance from center of city - type of population, unpaved streets, cheap houses.
This is a typical nego area, on the outskirts of the city. Sale demand is largely for investment and when prices are bargains.
All city conveniences, school and churches in area.
Type of population (some criminal element) cement plant-fertilizer factory and many other smaller industrial plants, many unpaved streets, inadequate transportation, very poor construction

10% type mentioned above is located on West Commerce West of Edgefield - the reason for the increase in value shown is that since 1929 a 4 Lane highway to Fort Worth has been opened just South of this section and has resulted in a better type of people moving into this particular section, modernization and repair of properties. Part of area North of railroad and east of Edgefield contains the lower grade of population and cheaper, poorly maintained properties.
Has all city conveniences, adequate transportation. School in area.
Fort Worth Highway through center of area along which is located tourist camps, small drink & lunch stands, illing stations. Unpaved streets.

Section south of Fort Worth Highway largely vacant. Part of area North of Highway contains residential development. Reason for increase in value since 1929 is fact that Fort Worth Highway was not opened until 1932 and prior to that time transportation facilities were inadequate and demand for property in this section was almost nil.
Uniformity of construction. All city conveniences.
Lack of transportation, distance to schools, churches and stores, and principal business center, but type of development and population offsets these influences.
Executives, business and professional men, capitalists.
Not sufficient rental to warrant estimate

This is a highly developed subdivision outside city limits which was particularly designed for expensive suburban homes. That part west highway 116 is of the very highest type containing many of homes in the edifice classification. Some expensive types of cottages in northeastern area.
School in area. All city conveniences. Fairly convenient to stores and churches. Bus transportation.
This is an area bordered on all sides by high class residential sections except north which is vacant and future development will be in keeping present area and surroundings. Has deed restrictions.
All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Schools in area. Close to business center. Dallas Country Club joins on Southeast.
Large number of duplexes in area. Some infiltration of lower grade in part of area south of Mocking Bird lane between St. L. Railroad & Douglas Street.
Executives, business and professional men capitalists & clerical
Very few for sale practically all result of purchase of vacant lot & erection by owner of house for individual taste
Not sufficient rental to warrant estimate

10% type above is located in Greenway Parks, one of the most beautifully platted additions in the south. It has beautiful landscaping, restricted to 1 structure per lot. Construction uniform, lot sizes large with beautiful parkways thru center of each block maintained by compulsory taxation. Part of area most likely to decline is south of Mockingbird Lane to railroad. Duplexes and apts. located from Normandy to Larchmont between Preston Road to railroad. Remainder of area uniform and substantial, North-eastern portion of area contains several expensive homes costing as much as 100,000.
All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Overlooks White Rock Lake. Golf and country club adjoining. Stores convenient to West side: Adequate restrictions.
Clerical, executives, business and professional men
Poor because of lack of rental units

The area from Gaston Ave. to its Northern point, except about 1 block bordering Abrams Road, is considered one of the highest type residential districts of Dallas, containing several homes costing as much as $60,000. This area is well platted and contains considerable natural beauty. Along Abrams Road and south of Gaston Ave. is desirable but cheaper than remainder of area and not as well platted.
Adequate transportation. All city conveniences. Community business center in area.
Some distance to city grade and high schools. Distance to principal business center. Poor approach to main business district. Surrounded on two sides by cheaper properties. Unpaved streets.
Best part of area is East of Superior Street. A well established area of small brick and frame cottages, well occupied, and evidencing pride of ownership.
Uniformity of construction. Conveniently located to school. Good approach. Bus transportation. All city conveniences.
Distance from center of city. Unproved area on west. No restrictions except zoning.
Clerical some business and professional men
A small well balanced area, containing a better type of improvements than surrounding area.
All city conveniences, good schools, adequate transportation. Business center in area. Close to Stevens Park and El Tivoli Golf Courses.
Many unpaved street, distance from principal business center of Dallas, mixture of low price poor construction.
Clerical, Professional skilled and unskilled laborers, executives

Section east of Oak Cliff Blvd. & North of Burlington best part of area. Much new construction south of Jefferson & west of Westmoreland, also north of Jefferson between Calumet & Francis also in part of area South of G. C & S.F. Railroad, also in Western part north of Davis Street. South of Davis & north of Jefferson between Kramer & Ravinnia not so good.
All city conveniences, grade schools & high school, churches and business center in area. Adequate transportation. Parks in area.
Mixed type of construction, older properties transition to business in center of area. Nothing but zoning restrictions in area, City Zoo in southeast corner.
Executives, business men, professional men, clerical, skilled and unskilled laborers
Apts.4/16 units 3/5 rs. This area also contains 3 hotel apts. in addition.

Private owned amusement park, containing swimming pool, dance pavilion, ball park and picnic grounds. Might be considered of no benefit to area in northern part. Small settlement of negroes also in northern part.
Clerical, business executives and professional men

Jefferson Ave. is largely business all through area and around its intersection with Beckley and Marsalis is several blocks are included in business. Marsalis, Beckley, and Bishop North of Jefferson predominate in apartments. Also many apartments in Kings Highway. Clinton, Winnetka, Willoment, Elsbeth, Zang Blvd., are better streets. The area is composed of almost every type of of property, good, bad and indifferent, single family, 2 story and apartments, cheap old houses, and more modern good houses, with predomination in older properties. As a whole the part of area North of Jefferson is better than the part South of Jefferson.
Has all city conveniences, schools and churches in area. Adequate transportation.
Mixture of population - proximity of river. Cemetery. Packing House in area, many cheap stores, street car barn in area, many unpaved streets.
Unskilled laborers, domestics, Packing house employees, street car employees
25 About 5% of area is 2 sty frames & apts. 4- fam. converted 3/4 rm. units

Cheaper properties located north of Hutchins. North of railroad east of Cliff and south of Hutchins includes a slightly better type of property. South of Hutchins and west of Cliff St. includes the larger better properties in the area, apartments and 2 stories.

School and churches in area. Community business center easily accessible. Adequate transportation, except Northern part which is served by Shuttle Bus connecting with street cars which is slightly inconvenient. Area touches municipal golf course on west. Has all city conveniences.

North end of Windomere, Edgefield, Clinton and Winnetka and west end of Neches, 5th & 6th, Salmon Drive, Thomasson, Steward, best streets. South part of western side oldest part of area. Apartment houses located principally along Kings Highway.
This is a small are of negro houses - occupants largely employed as domestics in adjoining areas to west. No expansion of area.
All city conveniences, schools and churches in area. Adequate transportation.
Mixed type of construction - railroad - many unpaved streets.
Clerical, laborers, skilled and unskilled some business m

New construction scattered all over area, southeast, central portion and eastern edge has most activity in new building. An area without any outstanding favorable or detrimental influences - but cheaply priced.
Uniformity of construction. Country Club and Golf Course joins on South. Has all city conveniences. High elevation.
Lack of adequate transportation. Distance to schools and churches and community business center. Loss of activity in subdivision.
A fairly uniform area started about 11 years ago but because of lack of promotional ability of subdividers, activity past few years has been almost dead.
Has all city conveniences, schools, churches and stores in area. Bus transportation.
Distance to principal business center. Unpaved streets. Interurban line through part of area.

Northern part east of Beckley better part of area. Higher priced new construction north of Vermont and between Marsalis & Ramsey. Cheaper new construction is west of Beckley. On Beckley at Iowa & Georgia bordering street car line is worst part of area.
Schools, churches, stores in area. Bus transportation.
Mixed type of construction - Unpaved streets - distance to principal business center of Oak Cliff and Dallas.
Clerical, skilled and unskilled laborers. Some business men.
New construction in northeast and scattered all over area. Recent construction of two new schools has added stability of this area.
Near White Rock Lake. Well planned subdivision originally highly restricted. Natural beauty. Bus transportation. Has all city conveniences.
Not sufficient rental property to create demand

Original developer of this subdivision committed suicide and for a few years activity was slow. However, by reason of deed restrictions, location, type of construction and natural beauty area will remain good, and present building activity will in all probability rapidly increase.
Adequate transportation. Grade school in area. Country Club and one small part and one large park join area. Community business center in area.
Heavy traffic on Gaston Avenue. Age of majority of improvements. Encroachment of apartment houses.
Executives, business and professional men, clerical
Northeastern part has most of smaller places and new construction. Apartments mostly on Reiger, Victor, Tremont & Worth. Monto Vista, Newell, Clermont, best streets.
All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Close to schools, churches, and business center. Uniform type of large, expensive homes.
Area almost entirely built up. Age of properties.
Not sufficient rental property to establish an estimate

This is the last part of a highly restricted addition to be improved, containing structures that could be classed as edifices, occupied by well to do families but on a slight down trend due to younger generation moving in areas of more modern construction.
Adequate transportation. Schools, churches and community business center in area. All city conveniences.
Age of construction and lower grade area to south - some business encroachment. Encroachment of apartment houses.
Clerical, business and professional men, skilled mechanics
Executives, business, and professional men, capitalists

East of Lindbergh and North border East of Greenville Ave. best part of area. Southwest corner worst part of area. Apartment houses scattered over entire area except from Llano to Richmond between Greenville and Lindbergh with very few West of Greenville Avenue.
Highland Park and University Park Dallas, Texas
All city conveniences-adequate transportation-schools and stores in area. Churches in area. Southern Methodist University in area. Dallas Country Club joins on West.
Distance to Principal business center. Age of properties in Southern part of area.
Southern part static Northern part possibly upward
Clerical, business and professional men - executives
$7500-Fair at price Good on new const.

Along Drexel Drive and St. Johns Drive located several large, expensive homes but old. Southern part of area original part of Highland Park and while properties are old they are still desirable. New construction largely North of Southern Methodist University, on East side of area, where several new subdivisions have been opened. Values have quite a tendency to increase in areas and North of Southern Methodist University but it is possible for values to be adversely affected by cheaper construction on the north.
All city conveniences. Adequate transportation. Well planned and highly restricted area. Modern business center in area. Close to schools. Dallas Country Club joins.

Major portion of this area contains beautiful parkways, ideally landscaped and maintained by promoters of the addition. It has beautiful curving streets and boulevards amply large to care for traffic. Rigidly restricted by deeds that several years yet to run.
Stevens Park joins on west. Wooded lots. Scenic beauty. Uniformity of construction. Shuttle bus transportation in western part. All city conveniences.
Northeastern part some distance to transportation. Also some distance to schools, churches, and stores.
Clerical, executives, business and professional men
Only few houses for rent and these in older part which is southeast part of area. Not sufficient to estimate.

This area is well platted, containing rather rigid restrictions, exceptional natural beauty, both in contour and trees, containing several expensive houses, some two or three costing as much as $30,000.
Stevens Park adjoining on South and East. Uniformity of construction. All city conveniences. Scenic beauty. Shuttle bus transportation. Well restricted.
Some distance to schools, churches and stores. Area joining on North is adjacent to Fort Worth cut off road, a heavy traffic artery lined with filling stations, small stores and tourist camps.
Executives, salesmen, business and professional men

This is a new subdivision with majority of construction during past five years. It is well laid out, has natural scenic beauty good elevation. Type of development and population offsets distance to schools, churches and stores.
Small park playground in area. Good Senior High School joins on east. Major portion of area comparatively new. Southwestern part some distance from stores.
Shuttle Bus transportation along Jefferson somewhat inconvenient. Distance to principal business center.

A fairly well balanced neighborhood, largely new and with fair prospects for some further development. Southern part of area north of Jefferson is very active now with new construction, and Western part of area south of Jefferson also very active.
Level. Lies along Saginaw River opposite Crow Island.
No city facilities -- except electricity. Lack of transportation.
No development between the Railroad and the River. Practically all village taxes are paid by the Consumers Power. Village is unincorporated.
Lack of city facilities, transportation, etc.
Very sparsely settled except in the southern portion.
All city facilities except in undeveloped section to the north.
Native white: skilled mechanics and laboring class.
One block, State Street, north -- better houses, approximately $5,000 to $6,500; balance smaller houses ($2,100 to $5,000).
Level. North Saginaw. Includes Penoyer Park.
All city facilities. Ample room for development.
Native white; white collar and skilled mechanics
Section: Union, Michigan, Cooper and Bond are above average ($6,000 to 8,500). Almost rates BLUE grade.
All city facilities. Restricted - as they go along.
Lower class surroundings. Heavy special assessments for improvements in some cases.
Level. Little built up except on State Street.
Native white. Skilled mechanics and laboring class
Many good old houses of good size along Court St. mixed with some business. Started in 1920 with few houses; rest built in 1928-1929; sold on small down-payments--many taken back.
All city facilities. Adjacent to center of the city.
Along Michigan Avenue a number of large old homes, with a few of moderate age. Balance of section, west of Bond, lesser age with mixture of small fairly modern houses approximately $3,000 to $5,000.
Level. Very little developed except in southeast portion.
Trend of desirable growth is in this direction. Partial water, sewers, etc.
Adjacent to old center of the city. All city facilities.
Native white; skilled mechanics, white collar and laboring
Substantial percent semi-modern. All have water, sewers, etc. -- inside toilets but no basements.
Native white; white collar skilled mechs
A few large houses. Small section along Brockway.
Level. Very small development of high grade.
All city facilities. Near schools, etc.
All city facilities. Adjacent to best residential neighborhood and Country Club.
Native white, white collar executives, etc.
Started in 1929. One built in 1929 by owner. 3 within the last year; 8 only all told.
Level. Golf side development. Finest residential area in the city.
All city facilities. Adjacent to Country Club. Restricted.
Native white; white collar; executives, etc.
One family units: stucco, brick and frame
Back section restricted to $6,500 homes; balance to $10,000. No special assessments.
Native white of white collar class

This section runs for a few blocks along Gratiot Avenue and covers Gratiot Court and Garden Lane. The houses along Gratiot Avenue are of a more mixed type and somewhat older than those on the two short streets which are quite homogenous and of good character.
Adjacent to factories which employ a large part of the inhabitants.

Better along Michigan Avenue. Superior St. to Greenwich and along Greenwich contains some very good new houses running up to as high as $25,000 and property is being accumulated by owners thereof with a view to having it become a restricted neighborhood; eventually, it may even deserve an "A" grade.
Age and obsolescence. Adjacent to industry.
Type of structures. Lack of city facilities and transportation.
A collection of shacks and very poor and dilapidated dwellings.
Level land. Lies along east bank of river in southern end of city.
One family, 5-6 Room Bungalows: approximately $2500 to $3800
General demand for 5-room bungalows. No basements.
Pride of home-ownership. Walking distance of many factories.
Almost all built by brokers on speculation for small down-payment from factory workers.
Main highway, and adjacence to important Chevrolet plant.
Low priced construction. Distance from schools and center of city. Lack of city facilities.
Native white of the skilled mech & laboring class

Larger houses on Genesee from Webber to City Limits. South of the City limits is a bungalow development of low price - approximately $1,500 to $2,000. Some houses on Harold Street and Fulton Street are selling for approximately $5,000 to $6,000.
On main highway. Fairly near the Chevrolet plant.
Lack of city facilities. Distance from center of the city, schools, etc.
Native white; skilled mechanics - laboring class.
A sub-division of low priced units. Started in 1920; lay dormant until 1928-29 -- sold lots at approximately $5,00 down. Few houses built.
Large lots: 180 x 800', approximately 12 homes. Occupied by descendants of lumbermen of wealth; one sale in 1934 for approximately $19,000 (cost $40,000.)
Adjacent to industry. Age and obsolescence.
A few good old houses along Washington Avenue of higher value.
All city facilities. Close to the center of the city.
Mixed. White collar, skilled mechanics and laboring class

Genesee is largely business, but contains a number of large houses of good size and substantial age. Jefferson also has a number of large old houses -- some of them still occupied by wealthy families. Section bounded by Jefferson, Phelon, Brown and Holland, better than average -- approximately $7,000 to $12,000.
Adjacent to City. All city facilities.
Encroachment of business and industry. Age obsolescence. Threat of negro invasion.
Old section. Formerly occupied largely by Railroad men when Pere Marquette R.R. Shops were more active. Some fine old homes on Jefferson.
Adjacent to center of city. All city facilities.
White - Mixed; skilled labor, laboring etc.
Adjacent to industry and center of city.

A number of Poles and those of Polish descent have moved into this section from the northern part of the city which is now all negro. A few negro families are located on Hartsuff from 11th to 13th Sts. Type of houses along 4th and 5th is somewhat better than the average.
One low-priced subdivision east of 23rd and south of James with no city facilities. Sold: approximately $100 down.
Age; type of dwellings and inhabitants.

Formerly Railroad men occupied this section. When negroes started coming into the neighborhoods, many houses were bought at high prices for rental to them.   ** This rental is for 3 or 4 families per house.
Graded and high school in area, also churches and community business center.  Adequate transportation.  All city conveniences.
Factories adjoin on north end; mixed type of population; cheap construction.

Along Warwood Avenue on south end of this area is located community business section. Hazlett Avenue, north of 25th Street is worst and Warwood Avenue best type of construction. East side of Warwood between 13th Avenue and 22nd. is decidedly better part of area, contains larger lots and houses and properties are well maintained, but very old. Remainder of area fairly uniform as to construction type.
Close to recreational park, school churches, community business center; adequate transportation; all city conveniences
Nothing to rent in this area

Older part of area is southern part from N. 16th Street to N. 21st Street and contains frame houses.  The part of area between N. 21st Street and N. 23rd Streets is the part more recently developed and is predominantly brick.  Area lies well, is above flood waters and while there is very little activity in sales it is one of the most desirable sections in Warwood.
Warwood Terrace part is on side and top of hill.  Western part is level.
Close to recreation park, schools, churches, community business center, adequate transportation, all city conveniences.

Warwood Terrace is new part of section.  It is on a very high elevation and about 15 houses have been built in past year in this part.  On Warwood Avenue are two large expensive homes, costing about $30,000 each and immediately in front of them and extending two blocks to river is vacant section one block wide which is owned by same parties that own the two large homes. Cheaper part of area is that along 11th Street.
Graded schools in area; close to high school, churches and community business center; all city conveniences; adequate transportation.
Factories in area; mixed type of population; west of Warwood Avenue subject to highest flood waters.
Best part of area is north of 6th Street.  South part contains mixed type of population; joins factories and has cheaper properties.
Adequate transportation, city conveniences, close to schools, churches and community business center.
Very cheap construction; low-class population, mixed; on side of hill and foundations insecure.
This area presents a very dilapidated appearance; on hill-side; unpaved streets; mixture of lower type of population.
None, except better area adjoining on west and section further east and outside city limits contains Wheeling Country Club and some nice residences.
No city sewerage. Distance to schools, churches and business centers.  Inadequate transportation.  Cheap construction.
Reason for drop from Green Area to Red area is that the boundary line of the Green area on the east of this area is a large private estate.
Close to schools and churches and community business center.  Adequate transportation - all city conveniences.
Executives, business and professional men - capitalists

Maple, Walnut and Poplar are about 100% built up, but still very good.  Several large estates in area especially in northern part.  Woodsdale is older section.  Future expansion will trend toward northern part of area.  "D" area to east of northern part is across creek and joins edge of large estate.  Undeveloped area on east side of Bethany Park Road is the side of high hill and very little development there, only scattered houses.
Level, except northeast and east which goes into hills.
All city conveniences; adequate transportation; graded school in area and high school not far distant.  Also short distance to Wheeling Park. Churches and community business center in area.

Area along creek west of National Road and from America Avenue to Lenox Avenue subject to flood in extremely high waters sufficient to create some sales resistence on properties nearest creek.  Open sewer also empties into creek.

Edgewood is older section but between Edington Lane and Elm North and South and Carmel Road and Edgewood Street east and west are some well-kept nice, large homes, and this is a very desirable part of area. On northeast side around Edgewood in the edge of the hills are many old cheaper places, poorly kept. In the southern part of the area Cypress and Greenwood Avenue are the best.  Pleasant Avenue fairly good and west of Pleasant Avenue is a decline. Lynwood Avenue and Carmel Road, south of Edgington Lane much below other part of area and taken by themselves would rate lower grade.
Graded school in area and large high school just across National Road from southwest corner of area.  Adequate transportation and not far distant from communtiy business center and churches.
Cemeteries adjoin area on south and west, but they are well kept and do not seem to be considered as a detrimental influence.
Located in this area are 2 apartments of 4 and 6 units which are owned by parties living in them.
Also 1 duplex and one 4-unit apartment that is rented.

Many large estates with expensive homes are located along National Road.  Eastern side of area goes into the hill.  Northern part best and latest development.  Romany Road and Rockledge Road contain higher priced homes in southern part of area.
All city conveniences and adequate transportation.  Not far distant from churches, schools, and community business center.
National Road through this area is zoned for business and apartment houses and many small business places now on it. Creek on south also adversely affects.
Packing house and foundry workers, tobacco factory workers & steel workers

Extreme western part on hillside.  A drift coal mine was formerly located in Glenwood Heights and it is difficult to get solid foundations for buildings.  Some depressions are visible now.  Leatherwood is best part of area although it is old.
All city conveniences, adequate transportation, graded school in area.
Packing Company plants in area and several smaller industrial plants. Business along National Road. Joins creek on south
Packing plant workers, clerical, mill workers
Very little change in this area in past 10 years.  Business along National Road and industrial plants in area.  Residential development along Fulton and Wine Streets.
West side level - eastern side goes into the hill.
Graded schools in area and large high school only a short distance.  Churches and community business center close by.  Adequate transportation.  All city conveniences.  Wheeling Park also adjoins.
Executives, business and professional men, capitalists

Some large estates and some of the most expensive homes in the city located in the area.  Meadow Estates adjoining creek is new subdivision and only few lots have as yet been sold in it.   Along National Road, both sides are high-priced properties.  Eastern side has the lower-priced properties.
Graded school in area and not far distant to high school, churches and community business center.  All city conveniences and adequate transportation.
Five negro families located in area, three on Springdale Avenue and two on Harding Avenue.
A fairly uniformly improved section of medium-priced homes adversely affected by the fact that 5 Negro families reside in the area.
Schools, churches, and community business center in area.  Adequate transportation and all city conveniences.

This was formerly a separate municipality known as Elm Grove.  On north side along National Road is quite a business section.  On west side of Kruger Street from Columbia Avenue to National Road is best part of area; next is east of Kruger Avenue, between Columbia and National Road, and extending to Stone Church St.  Remainder of area fairly uniform section of frame houses, old and only fairly well kept.
Not far distant from schools, churches and community business center.  Fair transportation.
Coal mine adjacent. Cheap construction. Creek and railroad track on south.
This is an area of cheaply built small homes, located in a little valley at the bottom of a high hill.  It is known as a sort of dumping ground.  Very little change in past 10 years.
Graded school in area and close to community business center, churches and adequate transportation.
Purchasers of lots get only surface rights. Has no city sewerage. Very few paved sidewalks and streets. Cheap construction.
Junior Avenue about the best street.  Area only slightly improved.
Grade school in northeast part of area.  Linsly private school for boys in northwest part of area.  Transportation only fair. Southern part some distance to community business center.
Creek joining on north. Railroad tracks running through southern part with grade crossing.  Cheap construction, especially in southeast and east near creek.
Clerical, factory workers, cheap laborers, loafers

Morningside is not recently developed part, it has about 15 dwellings of the better type.  It and Washington Avenue contain practically all the best homes in the area, and are far ahead of the remainder.  Property along creek on east subject to overflow in extra high waters.  Development along Valley View Avenue also fairly good.
West side level, up hill towards east.
Easy walking distance to principal business section.  Schools, churches and stores in area.  All city conveniences.
Age of properties; lower grade area surrounding small lots.
Clerical, professional business men and skilled mechanics

Chapline Street contains the better class of dwellings in the area.  Cheaper properties on Eoff Street.  The section is very old.  Homes concentrated on small lots. Proximity to principal business district is cause for good rental demand.
Schools, churches, stores located in area.  Adequate transportation.  All city conveniences.

Age of properties; mixture of population; restricted district along 23rd St. at River. Industrial plants located along river front and scattered throughout area. Western half also subject to flood waters from river. Railroad tracks through area.

This is a very mixed area, as to population and type of property.  The part south of 32nd Street is the better part but in this section are located many industrial plants employing cheaper labor and this part is also more subject to flood hazard.  The part between 32nd Street and extending northward is the older part and on the western side of this portion along Main Street is located many saloons and "dives" of every description.
Part along Main Street and 17th, 18th, and 19th Sts. fairly level and remainder of area goes from bottom of hill to almost the top.
Adjoins principal business district.  Negro and white schools in area, also churches and stores. Not subject to flood except at very tip of north end of area and there is nothing to be damaged.

North part along Chapline, parts of Market St., all of Lind, Grandview, Cherry, Vine, Summit, Isabelle, High, Charles and others on side of high hill and streets are very steep grades. Mixed type of population, R.R. tracks thru southern part. Industrial plants located along Wheeling creek and R.R. tracks, also on Main St.
Clerical, laborers, factory workers, business and professional men, skilled mechanics
Apts. consisting of more than 4 units 4-6 r

This area includes almost every type of old property and every type of population.  On Main St. between 7th and 9th Streets are some fairly nice 2-story brick row houses and one large apartment house.  Better houses and apartmentss also located along 12th Street.  Negro section on Market and Chapline out to about 7th Street and also on intersecting streets in this part.  It is about the most spotted area in the city.

Adequate transportation; schools and churches in area.  Community business center in area; all city conveniences.  Just across river from principal business section.  Breezes from the river make it pleasant place to live in summer.

Flood hazard; area under water from 1-10 feet in March, 1936, January, 1937, and April, 1937.  Age of properties.  Large number of places on market and practically no buyers except at big bargain prices.
Clerical, skilled mechanics, laborers, and professional men

About 25 years ago many prominent and wealthy citizens built expensive homes on the Island, and it was known as the "Garden Spot" and for years it was a desirable place in which to live, but in later years the frequency of floods has practically ruined the sales demand on the Island. The large and better homes are located on Front Street, and the smaller cheaper homes are on the other streets.  Proximity to principal business district and being cool in summer trend to make demand for rentals good, but flood hazard very seriously affects sales demand.
Adequate transportation, schools, churches and stores either in or adjoining area. All city conveniences. Proximity to principal business district.  Cool in summer.

Flood hazard.  This area is the lower part of the Island and more subject to overflow than northern end.  Area under water from 1-18 feet in March, 1936 and January and April, 1937. In recent years floods have been more frequent.  Properties old.

At south end of area is Horse Race Track, circus grounds, Wheeling High School football stadium.  Better part of area is in south of Zane Street for about 3 blocks on eastern side. Western side is low. Proximity to principal business section keeps up rental demand, but flood hazard and age of properties seriously affects sale demand.
Schools, churches and communtiy business center located in area.  Bus transportation but schedule not favorable.
Distance to center of city. Very hilly. Most streets paved with treated cinders -- not very satisfactory.  No city sewerage.
This is a small community located about 3 miles from the principal business section of Wheeling. It is located in the hills and is rather a healthy spot.
Utilities - adequate transportation to Denver - schools - nearby Fitzsimons Hospital (Army) which helps the rent situation.
High bonded debt - lack of restrictions - unpaved streets.

Area is the heart of Aurora, an incorporated town. Colfax Ave., in the center of area is dividing line between Arapahoe County on the south and Adams County on the north. Property in the Adams County section is heavily burdened with bonded debt for improvements, which is detrimental to property therein. Area is semi-agrarian and rural, occupied by gardeners and wage earners chiefly. Property is poorly kept, with unpaved streets except Colfax. There is very little sales demand but is good rent section because Fitzsimons Hospital (Army) is located in Aurora and is convenient to out of town visitors who come to be near kin folk confined to the Hospital. Mortgage lenders prefer to avoid this area except on a very conservative basis.

An area of small frame cottages occupied by a substantial class of low income wage earners, the kind who live within their incomes, even though small. These small houses sell readily from 1500 to 2500, terms of 10% down. Real estate men look for the area to improve and possibly build up with this type of small houses, with the establishment of the Army Air Corps Technical School to the south. It is expected that the lower income employees of the school, such as enlisted men, mechanics, will move to this area. Fitzsimons General Hospital (army) in nearby Aurora, has helped make this a good rent area.
Nearby park- nearby Army Flying School (calculated to stimulate sales and rents) all utilities, adequate transportation.

Very spotty, difficult to analyze. Before 1900 Count Richthoffen of Germany built a castle in what is now Richthoffen Place. Few country estates went up in the neighborhood. Some well-to-do health seekers located in area. Did not built rapidly but during last few years there has been a small amount of new construction of good bungalows costing up to $8000. New Amy Air Corps Tech. School to the southeast will undoubtedly bring about the construction of a large number of bungalows in the $6000-8000 class to house officers and higher income attaches of the field. A wide variety of houses in age, style and type, it is a good "B" because of the class of property which predominates.
Adequate schools- transportation - utilities. Nearby City Park, attractive 17th Ave. Parkway, Monaco Blvd. and Montview Blvd. in area
Very few rent houses available from $60-125

This is the newer part of the choice Park Hill section. 17th Ave. Parkway in the area is one of the very attractive boulevards of the city. Monaco Blvd. and Montview Blvd. in the area are two other boulevards artistically landscaped, and built up on both sides with the better class of homes. Although some of the houses on East 17th Ave. Parkway and Montview Blvd. are 20-25 years old, they maintain their character of exclusiveness and desirability. The fact that the area is "Park Hill" adds to its desirability.
All utilities- adequate transportation- schools- churches.

This outer fringe of the Park Hill section is newer than B-2. The vacant ground to the north and cast offers unlimited opportunity for future building. The area has built slowly away from the heart of the Park Hill section (B-2) and naturally houses near B-2 are older. The area is occupied by a moderate income group- white collar people, clerks and small business men. A good "B" lacking the "tone and exclusiveness" of A-1 and A-2. An appreciable amount of new construction would make the outer fringe an "A". It is not too spotty to class first grade, but it is a very good "B".
Adjoining Cheesman Park and Golf Course- good schools in area- churches - good transportation - all utilities.
Good- Some 5% reductions in rent during first one half of 1938

The heart of Park Hill section, long considered one of the most desirable in Denver, the "elite" section for many years. Although it is built up with some houses 25 years old, it continues to hold its desirability, chiefly because of schools, proximity to City Park and partly because it is "Park Hill." Older house are usually well reconditioned. 17th Parkway is a wide thoroughfare, beautifully kept, but houses between Colorado Blvd. and Dexter are too old to be graded "A". A good sales demand prevails. It is a very good rent district. Still considered the best residential section of Denver by many "moderate income" business and professional people. A good B area.
Schools are across two heavy traffic highways (Colfax and Colorado Blvd.) for those residing south of Colfax.

A sooty section with newer houses south of Colfax bordering A-2. The security between Batavia and Colfax is older and inferior. Colfax Ave. east of Colorado Blvd. is dotted with business houses. A fair demand for houses exists but buyers much prefer to select houses in older adjoining B-2. One reason is the school situation. A fair "B".
Adequate transportation- utilities- churches. Community Center on Colfax.

An attractive bungalow area, virtually all of which has been built since 1929. Houses are uniform in style, size and quality. The vacant area to the east and south will undoubtedly build up with a substantial type of brick bungalow. While this area does not rank with A-1, 3, 4, and 5 in the size or cost of homes, it stands out as the best moderately-price new section of Denver.
Nearby Golf Course and City Park- adequate transportation- all utilities.

30 new houses of the $4000-4800 class were built on Milwaukee and Fillmore between 29th and 33rd during the first half of 1938. Were largely FHA financed and bought by wage earners with small down payments. Area is spotty with many older houses. Better paid wage earners from nearby industrial plants occupy it and help make sales and rent situation favorable. Bordering the Golf Course between St. Paul and Colorado Blvd. are large new expensive structures, but this better section is too small to classify separately. As a whole is a good working mans' area, where there is likely to be more new building of cheaper type.
Negro and foreign infiltration- commercial encroachments.

This section, bordering the heavy commercial district to the west and northwest, is an old area now occupied by a combination of Negroes, Mexicans and a transient class of workers. The west and northwest part of it is Denver's closest approach to a slum district. Shacks, largely held by speculators, rent for as low as $5 per month. Negroes occupy the eastern and better part of the area. Cheap houses in the area have a good rental demand. A poor 4th grade section.
All utilities- adequate transportation- schools- churches.
NOTE: Terraces are rows of apts- investment property entirely.

This is a better Negro section of Denver and is one of the best colored districts in the United States. The northeastern part of it is often referred to as the "Negro Country Club". It is an old brick section with a reasonably large number of well-kept newer houses, mostly occupied by Negroes. It is not a typical Negro area of cheap, tumble-down ill-kept shacks found in eastern and mid-western cities, but all of the colored occupants are housed in brick structures- either detached or in terraces. For a Negro section it is very well kept up. Were it not for the heavy colored population much of it could be rated "C". In financing home ownership, the better class negroes usually obtain loans from institutions; but others are victims of industrial operators who have high fees and high interest rates.
East of Pennsylvania, level; west of Pennsylvania to Broadway, is on a hill.
Schools, utilities, adequate transportation; churches, close in.

Forty to 50 yrs. ago this was in the swank "Capitol Hill" areas, occupied by Denver's leading families. The mansions of that day have turned to clubs, rooming houses and made-over apartments, to a greater extent than any other area of Denver. Being close-in it is perfectly suited to this type of usage. The large old homes are also being turned to business houses. It is also an apartment district. A good substantial class of clerks and office people live in the rooming houses and apartments. The area, turning commercial, should display good ground values in the future.
East High School in area, City Park, Business houses on East Colfax- Schools- all utilities, adequate transportation.

An area of 2-story houses for which there is now no active demand. The better part of the area is that east of Monroe, where the security is newer. The area is occupied by a large number of original owners of houses ranging in age from 25 years up, and is beginning to witness transition to rooming houses in the west end; also some commercial encroachments other than those near Colfax, which is a business street. A typical the good 3rd grade section which is due to decline in the future because of the age of the properties.
Nearby 7th Ave. Parkway- all utilities- adequate transportation- good schools.

This is a high assessment section. The houses within a block of the boundaries of A-4 are high grade, well kept structures bordering on first grade Nearer 10th Ave. they are older. The area as a whole enjoys a favorable reflex from particularly 7th Ave. and its attractive parkway. Were it not that the sections nearest 7th Ave. are entirely built up and above 10 years old, they could properly be classed first grade. A very good second grade area which will retain its character for several years.
Beautifully landscaped parkway in center of wide street, all utilities, adequate transportation, schools, churches, nearby Cheesman Park.

Although 7th Ave. Parkway almost entirely built up, with some houses 15 yrs old, it would be odd to visualize the city without this section, classed A or among the very best. With 7th Ave. Parkway and beautifully kept yards, it is indeed an outstanding section of better class homes, housing some of Denver's wealthiest, most affluent citizens. Strangely, the cemetery abutting 3 1/2 blocks between Cheesman Park and York, has made no difference to the desirability of the adjoining section. There is an exclusiveness about the area that helps to sustain values. It will hold its character for several years. Many of Denver's finest homes are in this area. Lenders advised that the security herein is acceptable for as high a ratio and as long in periods as new A-3 and A-6.
Dumping grounds north of Cherry Creek.

Trend in better home construction definitely to this area, with much vacant ground north and south for expansion -restricted- utilities and adequate transportation. Park in the southwest part of area- school facilities.
None outstanding except the uncertain influence of the nearby Army Air Corps Technical School.
All owner-occupied except new houses for sale

Denver's most intense activity in construction of the better type of houses is centered in this area. Crestmoor Addition (east of Holly, south of 6th) developed by Garrett-Bromfield, is a well planned sub-division wherein newly built houses are selling for $10, 500 to 29,000. The section surrounding Mountain View Park is being built up with substantial structures running from $7000 to $15,000. The lower priced houses (as low as $5500) are being put up north of 6th between Colorado Blvd. and Fairfax. It is a new area entirely, and Crestmoor is Denver's newest high priced subdivision. A house recently sold to Jew in Crestmoor brought summary action in barring the builder from future work in the area. The undeveloped land to the south offers great possibilities of future development. Since the area was begun, three to four years ago, the Army Air Corps Technical School has been located a short distance to the southeast. The extent to which this will be detrimental to the exclusive area cannot yet be estimated. The trend is definitely to this area, including the undeveloped sections on the north and south of it. The new development in the southwest part of this area began in full view and knowledge of the poor houses in C-9 and D-2. A-3 is on higher ground than D-2 and C-9 and Colorado Blvd. which divides them, is a wide thoroughfare, something of a natural barrier. With respect to adjoining D-2 and C-9, it can only be said that high priced houses are being built and sold in the southwest part of A-3.

This is a very trashy part of Harman, once a separate village. All of the houses border on shacks, streets are unpaved, and the entire southern part of the area is being used as dumping grounds to fill in along Cherry Creek. Area is lower in elevation than A-3 to the east. A-3 and A-5 were both developed with the full knowledge of this cheap area. Developers and real estate men have looked forward to buying up cheap houses in this area for newer development, should the trend to the northeastern part of Denver be sufficiently strong to warrant it. A cheap and poor section.
Slightly irregular, slopes to west. Lower ground than A-3 across street.
Fair, a good cheap rent area

All of this area and portions of the adjoining area north and south was once in the village of Harman. It is very spotty with some good bungalows and other old houses of varying size and type. There are a number of Negroes in area, mostly home owners. Efforts to dislodge them have failed because they've lived there many years. A-3 on the east and A-5 on the west were both developed with full knowledge of the conditions existing in C-9. D-2 on the south is a very trashy section. This area has rather an odd relationship to A-3 and A-5, which appears not to affect the 1st grade sections. While spotty, the cheaper and older security predominates and it could be considered at best only a "fair to poor" 3rd grade area.
An exclusiveness which helps sustain values, all utilities, restrictions, good transportation. County Club on south.
Adjoining C and D areas on the east, and several Negro families on 3rd Ave. west of York.

South of 4th in this area is the exclusive Country Club. The older part of the Country Club is that west of High. Although some of the structures are 25 years old, the area seems to maintain its character, being a concentration of the social elect. North of 4th and east of High is the exclusive Park Lane Square district created 10 years ago by purchase and demolition of cheap houses, some of which were occupied by Negroes. In the heart of this Addition is the half million dollar palatial home of Mrs. Verner Z. Reed. It was the plan to join this area with Country Club to the south, but the economic depression
Irregular- slopes downward in west end and upward in eastern part.
Inferior C-9 to the south with some Negroes.

An area of small brick bungalows, serving something as a buffer between the better B-5 and the spotty C-9 on the south. There is a possibility that the type of houses in this area will crowd into C-9. The area is occupied by a modest income group. Real estate men expect a continued demand for the type of property therein. A "fair B".
Ascends a hill in vicinity of 8th.
All utilities- adequate transportation- schools- churches- Chessman Park
About 20 doubles and a few apts. in area

Except for the small portion of this area south of 4th, it is a district of large 2-story houses; considered an exclusive section 20 to 25 years ago when it  was occupied by Denver's leading citizens. The area is attractive with its large shade trees and well maintained yards, and houses. Because of a certain exclusiveness that attaches to the area it would be too harsh to call it a "C", but because of the age and style of the houses it is bound to decline. This is evidenced by the poor sales demand.
Close in- all utilities- churches, adequate transportation.
All investment property- terraces and apts. Very few dbls.

An apartment house areas, serving somewhat as a buffer between the commercial area and the better C-7. Close in, it was the ideal section for the building of apartments, 15 to 20 years ago when it had begun to decline as a residential district. Is the western "base" of the Capitol Hill section. Its large, old houses were once among the best in Denver; new rooming houses. As in C-7 these have declined precipitously in value in 1929. Three or four new apartments have been built in the area in the last two years. The trend will be to more apartments. A very good rent area.
Northern one-half level; southern part rolling.
All utilities- adequate transportation, schools, parks, close to South Broadway industrial and commercial plants.

Another wage earners' section with houses a little inferior in quality to those of C-10 and C-11. The area is spotty. In the south end east of Broadway are large old 2-story houses. Some small houses and a few terrace apts. were built in the center of the area in 1937, all designed for low income occupants. Newer houses sell for $4,000, older ones up to $3250. Railroad tracks at northern boundary are being replaced with a boulevard. Near the city limits in the southern part of the area are a number of gardens, small farms. A "fair to average C".
Close in, with Broadway retail district in the area- All utilities, adequate transportation, schools.
None (a few of terrace apts. built in 1937)

The reasonably large south Broadway business district, the Ford Plant, and its proximity to the downtown section, contributed to make this a very good rental section. It is a wage earners' district entirely. East of Broadway small 4 and 5 room houses predominate. The section west of Broadway is older than that cast of Broadway, bordering no a "D" grade. A spotty district, it is a fair "C".
Schools- Utilities- Adequate transportation. Proximity to Washington Park.

Farther removed from Broadway with its business, industrial and heavy traffic, and close to Washington Park, this area is more desirable than C-10. Houses are larger, more substantial and uniformly better in every way. The better houses are on the eastern fringe. The area has a much better grade of 2-family structures than C-10. Occupied by persons in a wide variety of occupations- small income, business and professional, clerks, mail carriers, barbers, etc., it is a good "C'.
Nearby Denver University- all utilities, schools, adequate transportation.
Lacking street improvements in part of area.

An area where small frame houses predominate, this being out of the zone restricted to fire proof houses. Occupied by a substantial class of clerks, wage earners and the like, the appearance of yards indicates pride of ownership. Close to Denver University, it is a choice rent section, also a good one for sales. Were the houses generally larger and more substantial this would rate a "B" grade. Some of the streets are unpaved but will soon be oiled. The sparsely built up portion on the south will build up with small houses.
